title: Senior Technical Account Manager (Strategic Alliances)
description:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter-giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.
 As a Senior Technical Account Manager (Senior TAM, L6) at Affirm, you will own the operational aspect of technical account management across Affirm's strategic alliance portfolio-alerting, monitoring, troubleshooting, delivering against SLAs, fielding technical inquiries, and performing investigations and analysis, while also driving technical initiatives that translate merchant business objectives into technical strategies and product optimizations. Senior TAMs are part of the Engineering team and collaborate closely with Affirm's Product, Engineering, Operations, Customer Success, and Frontline Technical Support teams.
 This is an operations-heavy role to start. Expect the majority of your early focus to be on keeping merchant integrations healthy-monitoring, triage, troubleshooting, and SLA delivery-while you progressively take on more custom solutioning and cross-functional initiatives. Over your first 6-12 months, as you build operational mastery, you will grow into owning your own book of accounts and carrying it through to end-to-end account ownership.
 A Senior TAM independently owns operational health across the strategic alliance portfolio, designs custom integration solutions grounded in Affirm's standard integrations, drives cross-team collaboration on initiatives, acts as a technical lead on team projects, and mentors less-experienced members of the team.
 What You'll Do
 Own the operational aspect of technical account management across Affirm's strategic alliance portfolio-alerting, monitoring, troubleshooting, and fielding technical inquiries-so integrations stay healthy and issues are resolved quickly.
 Deliver against SLAs, proactively surfacing technical risks before they become customer-impacting and responding with urgency to merchant issues.
 Perform in-depth investigations and root-cause analysis across logs, queries, and integration data, owning resolution end to end and escalating to cross-functional partners or executives when needed.
 Drive technical initiatives and partner with internal and merchant stakeholders on launch initiatives-expansions, promotions, new product adoption, and integration optimizations-that grow the value of the accounts after launch.
 Design and deliver high-scope, often-custom integration solutions grounded in Affirm's standard integrations-combining, extending, and tailoring them to complex, open-ended problems while balancing speed, quality, maintainability, reliability, and scalability.
 Act as a technical lead for internal projects, defining and delivering well-scoped milestones and executing the project roadmap.
 Operationalize best practices by creating and updating playbooks, runbooks, alerting, and UAT certification plans across the strategic alliance portfolio and continuously reduce keep-the-lights-on (KTLO) work.
 Partner with Product and Engineering leads to identify, plan, and prioritize projects based on team goals and resources, acting as the voice of the merchant to influence the roadmap.
 Mentor and level up less-experienced TAMs, share learnings from your integrations and investigations, and contribute to interviewing and team development.
 Over your first 6-12 months, grow into owning a dedicated book of strategic alliance accounts-carrying operational ownership through to end-to-end account ownership.
 What We Look For
 Professional Background: at least six years in a technical, external-facing role such as Technical Account Management, Solutions/Partner Engineering, or Solutions Architecture-ideally within FinTech, payments, or SaaS-with a demonstrated track record of owning the operational health of technical accounts and delivering against SLAs.
 Operational Ownership: proven ability to run alerting, monitoring, troubleshooting, and technical inquiries across a set of accounts, balancing reactive operational work with proactive initiatives.
 Ownership & Autonomy: proven ability to independently scope and deliver complex, open-ended technical work, and to partner with stakeholders on launch initiatives, with strong project management and follow-through.
 API Expertise: deep understanding of RESTful APIs, webhooks, and the HTTP protocol, with hands-on experience using tools like Postman to debug and validate integrations.
 Architecture Fluency: Experience in API integrations and the ability to design custom solutions on top of them to solve complex merchant challenges.
 Coding & Code Fluency: ability to read and understand production-level code (HTML, JavaScript, SQL, and ideally one server-side language such as Python) and to author new, novel queries to diagnose merchant or system issues.
 Troubleshooting Acumen: ability to diagnose issues using browser developer consoles, log analysis and observability platforms (e.g., Snowflake, Chronosphere), and ticketing systems (e.g., Jira, Notion).
 Technical Communication: excellent verbal and written communication; able to tailor explanations to both non-technical leaders and technical teams, read a room and adjust in real time, and synthesize technical challenges back to internal teams.
 Relationship Management: ability to discover and develop relationships with technical decision-makers, secure written consensus on integration milestones, and drive cross-team collaboration.
 Leadership & Mentorship: demonstrated ability to mentor teammates, set best practices, and lead technical initiatives; a growth mindset with self-awareness and a habit of seeking and acting on feedback.
 Nice to Have
 Familiarity with the payments ecosystem.
 Familiarity with web/mobile application architecture.
 Experience implementing or customizing e-commerce platforms, payment gateways, or in-store point-of-sale systems.
 Experience acting as a technical lead on cross-functional projects and influencing product roadmaps.
 Pay Grade - L
Equity Grade - 4
Employees new to Affirm typically come in at the start of the pay range. Affirm focuses on providing a simple and transparent pay structure which is based on a variety of factors, including location, experience and job-related skills. 
Base pay is part of a total compensation package that may include monthly stipends for health, wellness and tech spending, and benefits (including 100% subsidized medical coverage, dental and vision for you and your dependents). In addition, the employees may be eligible for equity rewards offered by Affirm Holdings, Inc. (parent company).
CAN base pay range per year: $133,000 - $183,000
 Location - Remote Canada
 This remote role is open only to candidates residing in Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia, Ontario, Prince Edward Island, or Saskatchewan.
 #LI-Remote 
 Remote-first with flexibility built in 
 Affirm is proud to be a remote-first company. Most roles can be done from almost anywhere within the country of employment. Some positions may occasionally require in-person work at an Affirm office, and a few are office-based due to the nature of the work. All new hires will be invited to attend an in-person onboarding experience.
 Benefits designed for you 
 Our benefits reflect our commitment to care, transparency, and flexibility. Here are a few highlights:
 Health coverage at no cost: We cover 100% of premiums for employees and their dependents.
 Spending stipends: Monthly stipends support your tech setup, and the ability to choose health and wellness options that are right for you.
 Time off to recharge: Flexible time off and generous holiday calendars help you rest when you need to.
 Own a piece of what you build: Our employee stock purchase plan (ESPP) lets you buy Affirm stock at a discount.
 We're committed to providing an inclusive interview process, including accommodations for candidates with disabilities. If you need support, we're happy to help.
 For positions based in San Francisco or Los Angeles: Affirm considers qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, as required by law.
 By clicking "Submit Application," you acknowledge that you have read Affirm's Global Candidate Privacy Notice and consent to the use of your personal information as described.

title: Senior Program Manager, Compliance
description:
Who We Are 
 At Justworks, you'll enjoy a welcoming and casual environment, great benefits, wellness program offerings, company retreats, and the ability to interact with and learn from leaders in the startup community. We work hard and care about our most prized asset - our people. 
 We're helping businesses get off the ground by enabling them to focus on running their business. We solve HR issues. We're data-driven and never stop iterating. If you'd like to work in a supportive, entrepreneurial environment, are interested in building something meaningful and having fun while doing it, we'd love to hear from you. 
 We're united by shared goals and shared motivations at Justworks. These are best summed up in our company values, which are reflected in our product and in our team. 
 Our Values 
 If this sounds like you, you'll fit right in. 
 Who You Are 
 Justworks is seeking a Senior Program Manager, Compliance to lead planning, governance, and execution across the Product Compliance portfolio. You thrive in highly regulated environments where priorities evolve quickly and complex work spans multiple teams. You understand compliance, risk, controls, and operations-not necessarily because you're the deepest subject matter expert in every area, but because you know how to bring the right experts together and translate complex priorities into action. You are equal parts strategic planner, program leader, and operational problem solver. You bring structure to ambiguity, connect work across teams, identify risks and dependencies early, and create the transparency and accountability needed to drive complex initiatives through completion. You are comfortable partnering across Compliance, Operations, Product, Engineering, Accounting, Finance, Legal, Internal Audit, Security, and other teams to strengthen compliance while enabling the business to scale.
 Your Success Profile 
 What You Will Work On 
 Drive the Product Compliance Portfolio
 Develop and maintain an integrated view of Product Compliance priorities, initiatives, milestones, dependencies, and risks.
 Partner with Product Compliance leadership to prioritize work based on regulatory risk, business impact, dependencies, and available capacity.
 Translate priorities into executable plans with clear ownership, sequencing, milestones, and outcomes.
 Establish planning and reporting rhythms that provide leadership with visibility into progress, risks, dependencies, and areas requiring intervention.
 Drive initiatives through completion and ensure identified issues are tracked to sustainable resolution.
 Lead Complex Cross-Functional Programs
 Lead complex programs that span Product Compliance and cross-functional partners, particularly where successful outcomes require coordinated changes across Operations, Product, Engineering, Accounting, Finance, Legal, Internal Audit, or other teams.
 Drive program structure, planning, coordination, execution, and escalation while partnering with subject matter experts who retain responsibility for substantive compliance decisions.
 Identify dependencies, risks, resource constraints, and blockers early and work across teams to resolve them.
 A key near-term priority will be driving execution of the Compliance Risk & Remediation program, including coordinating remediation across Product Compliance and cross-functional partners and establishing governance to track identified issues through resolution.
 Build Product Compliance Governance
 Establish scalable governance for Product Compliance initiatives, including intake, prioritization, ownership, milestone tracking, risk and dependency management, escalation, and executive reporting.
 Develop repeatable operating rhythms that strengthen accountability and transparency across the portfolio.
 Create clear mechanisms for surfacing risks, decisions, and areas requiring leadership or cross-functional support.
 Strengthen the Product Compliance Operating Model
 Partner with Product Compliance leadership and subject matter experts to strengthen the operating model, including clarity of roles, responsibilities, and ownership.
 Improve documentation and business continuity across critical compliance processes and support sustainable control implementation.
 Develop meaningful measures of compliance performance, risk, and execution, while reducing single points of failure across the function.
 Enable Operational Excellence
 Identify and help drive opportunities to simplify workflows, reduce manual and duplicate work, strengthen quality and controls, and improve regulatory response and execution.
 Increase automation and leverage technology and AI where appropriate to improve efficiency, scalability, and sustainability.
 Measure Success
 Develop dashboards and executive reporting that provide visibility into portfolio health, remediation status, milestones, dependencies, compliance risks, control implementation, KPIs, and capacity considerations.
 Provide Product Compliance leadership with actionable insights and recommendations, including where priorities, resources, or cross-functional support may need to shift.
 How You Will Do Your Work 
 As a Senior Program Manager, Compliance, how results are achieved is paramount for your success and ultimately results in our success as an organization. In this role, your foundational knowledge, skills, abilities and personal attributes are anchored in the following:
 Strategic Planning - Develop roadmaps and execution plans that balance regulatory and risk priorities with business objectives and organizational capacity.
 Program Leadership - Lead multiple complex initiatives while maintaining clarity on priorities, ownership, dependencies, and outcomes.
 Systems Thinking - Understand how compliance, risk, technology, operations, controls, and business processes intersect across the organization.
 Operational Excellence - Build scalable ways of working that improve execution and efficiency while strengthening compliance.
 Risk Management - Identify program risks and dependencies early, develop mitigation strategies, escalate appropriately, and proactively remove blockers.
 Cross-Functional Influence - Build trusted partnerships and drive outcomes across technical and business teams without direct authority.
 Executive Communication - Translate complex program status, risks, dependencies, and tradeoffs into concise executive updates and recommendations.
 Continuous Improvement - Identify opportunities to improve processes, controls, automation, and operating maturity across Product Compliance.
 In addition, all Justworkers focus on aligning their behaviors to our core values known as COGIS. It stands for:
 Camaraderie - Day to day you can be seen working together toward a higher purpose. You like to have fun. You're an active listener, treat people respectfully, and have a strong desire to know and help others.
 Openness - Your default is to be open. You're willing to share information, understand other perspectives, and consider new possibilities. You're curious, ask open questions, and are receptive to thoughts and feedback from others.
 Grit - You demonstrate grit by having the courage to commit and persevere. You're committed, earnest, and dive in to get the job done well with a positive attitude.
 Integrity - Simply put, do what you say and say what you'll do. You're honest and forthright, have a strong moral compass, and strive to match your words with your actions while leading by example.
 Simplicity - Be like Einstein: “Everything should be made as simple as possible, but no simpler.”
 Qualifications 
 Required
 8+ years of program management, compliance operations, operational excellence, or related experience
 5+ years leading complex cross-functional initiatives
 Experience working in a highly regulated environment such as payroll, HR technology, financial services, fintech, or a similarly complex industry
 Demonstrated experience translating complex regulatory, risk, operational, or control priorities into structured programs and executable plans
 Experience leading programs that require coordination across multiple business and technical functions
 Demonstrated success building roadmaps, governance processes, and executive reporting
 Experience working with risk, compliance, internal controls, audit, or remediation programs
 Strong ability to influence and drive outcomes across teams without direct authority
 Exceptional organizational, analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills
 Ability to operate effectively through ambiguity and competing priorities
 Preferred
 Experience in payroll, payroll tax, SaaS, PEO, fintech, or HR technology environments
 Experience leading compliance, risk, control, or regulatory remediation programs
 Experience with operational or process transformation
 Experience partnering with Product and Engineering teams on complex operational or compliance initiatives
 Experience with AI-enabled workflow automation or other technology-enabled process improvements
 Familiarity with enterprise risk
 The base wage range for this position based in our New York City Office is targeted at $121,000.00 - $151,000.00 per year.

 Actual compensation is based on multiple factors that are unique to each candidate, including and not limited to skill set, level of relevant experience, and specific work location. Salary ranges for positions based in other locations may differ based on the cost of labor in that location. 
 For more information about Justworks' Total Reward Philosophy, including all of the perks and benefits we are proud to offer our team members, please visit Total Rewards @ Justworks .

 Justworks is committed to maintaining a workplace where diversity of identity, culture, and life experience is the norm and is celebrated authentically and respected consistently. Diversity in our work, our people, and our product drives creativity and innovation, entrepreneurial leadership and integrity, competitiveness, and collaboration throughout our business and in the market.  You're a seasoned compliance leader who knows that strong regulatory functions depend on clear ownership, capable teams, disciplined execution, and sound judgment. You bring meaningful experience leading regulatory compliance operations in a highly regulated environment. You can translate complex requirements into practical processes, challenge and support subject matter experts, and build the management systems needed to execute regulatory obligations consistently. You are equally comfortable developing teams, engaging with regulators and external partners, partnering with Legal and business leaders, and communicating risks and priorities to senior leadership. You enjoy strengthening functions that are evolving, creating clarity where processes or ownership are fragmented, and building a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
 Your Success Profile 
 What You Will Work On 
 Lead Regulatory Compliance and Licensing 
 Provide people and operational leadership across Regulatory Compliance and Licensing Operations within Product Compliance.
 Set clear priorities, ownership, operating rhythms, and performance expectations across the functions.
 Develop team members and build the capabilities, judgment, and accountability needed for consistent regulatory execution.
 Partner with Product Compliance leadership on organizational design, resourcing, and the continued evolution of these functions.
 Strengthen the Operating Foundation 
 Establish clear ownership, documented processes, effective controls, escalation paths, and backup coverage for critical regulatory obligations.
 Reduce single points of failure through cross-training, business continuity planning, and sustainable knowledge management.
 Improve visibility into upcoming obligations, execution status, risks, and issues requiring leadership attention.
 Standardize and simplify workflows where doing so improves reliability, efficiency, and compliance outcomes.
 Develop meaningful operational measures that help assess execution, capacity, quality, and risk.
 Drive Regulatory Execution and Readiness 
 Ensure timely, accurate, and compliant execution of key obligations, including PEO and other applicable licensing, CPEO certification, ESAC accreditation, regulatory reporting, government filings, business registrations, regulatory examinations, and agency correspondence.
 Ensure regulatory obligations are appropriately documented, calendared, assigned, reviewed, and escalated.
 Oversee interactions with regulators, government agencies, auditors, and external partners as appropriate, and ensure follow-up actions are completed.
 Identify emerging regulatory and operational risks early and ensure appropriate mitigation and escalation.
 Lead Regulatory Change 
 Lead the function in monitoring and interpreting relevant regulatory developments and assessing their impact on Justworks' products and operations.
 Ensure changes are communicated to the appropriate stakeholders and translated into clear operational, product, or control requirements.
 Partner with Payroll Compliance, Legal, Product, Engineering, Operations, and other stakeholders to support implementation of new or changing requirements.
 Establish clear processes for tracking regulatory change from identification through assessment, ownership, implementation, and closure.
 Strengthen Controls and Remediation 
 Partner with Product Compliance leadership, Internal Audit, Legal, Finance, Product, Security, and other stakeholders to strengthen controls and address identified risks within the functions.
 Support audit and examination readiness through clear documentation, evidence, ownership, and timely follow-up.
 Ensure remediation actions owned by the functions are appropriately prioritized, assigned, tracked, and sustained.
 Promote proactive risk identification and escalation rather than reliance on reactive issue management.
 Partner Across the Business 
 Build trusted partnerships across Legal, Product, Engineering, Payroll Compliance, Finance, Security, Internal Audit, Customer Success, Government Affairs, and Operations.
 Serve as a senior advisor on regulatory requirements, operational impacts, risks, and implementation considerations.
 Work with cross-functional partners to ensure regulatory requirements are understood and translated into practical, sustainable business processes.
 Build and Develop the Team 
 Build an engaged, high-performing team with clear expectations, strong accountability, and a culture of collaboration.
 Coach and develop team members, strengthen bench depth, and create opportunities for growth.
 Assess capabilities and capacity, address performance or skill gaps, and inform hiring and resourcing decisions.
 Create sustainable coverage across critical responsibilities through thoughtful role design, cross-training, and succession planning.
 How You Will Do Your Work 
As Senior Manager, Regulatory Compliance and Licensing, how results are achieved is paramount for your success and ultimately results in our success as an organization. In this role, your foundational knowledge, skills, abilities, and personal attributes are anchored in the following:
 Strategic Leadership - Set direction for the functions you lead and translate Product Compliance priorities into clear operational plans.
 People Leadership - Build, coach, and develop teams while establishing clear expectations and accountability.
 Regulatory Judgment - Apply strong regulatory and compliance judgment, know when deeper subject matter expertise is required, and ensure risks are appropriately evaluated and escalated.
 Operational Excellence - Build reliable, scalable processes, controls, documentation, and operating rhythms that reduce operational risk.
 Systems Thinking - Understand how regulatory requirements, licensing, product development, legal interpretation, controls, and operations intersect.
 Risk Management - Identify regulatory, operational, and business continuity risks early and drive practical mitigation.
 Cross-Functional Influence - Build trusted partnerships and drive outcomes across teams without relying solely on direct authority.
 Executive Communication - Provide clear, concise updates on regulatory priorities, organizational health, risks, and decisions requiring leadership attention.
In addition, all Justworkers focus on aligning their behaviors to our core values known as COGIS. It stands for:
 Camaraderie - Day to day you can be seen working together toward a higher purpose. You like to have fun. You're an active listener, treat people respectfully, and have a strong desire to know and help others.
 Openness - Your default is to be open. You're willing to share information, understand other perspectives, and consider new possibilities. You're curious, ask open questions, and are receptive to thoughts and feedback from others.
 Grit - You demonstrate grit by having the courage to commit and persevere. You're committed, earnest, and dive in to get the job done well with a positive attitude.
 Integrity - Simply put, do what you say and say what you'll do. You're honest and forthright, have a strong moral compass, and strive to match your words with your actions while leading by example.
 Simplicity - Be like Einstein: “Everything should be made as simple as possible, but no simpler.”
 Qualifications 
 Required 
 10+ years of progressive experience in regulatory compliance, licensing, tax compliance or research, compliance operations, or a related field.
 5+ years of people leadership experience, including leading teams responsible for complex regulatory or compliance obligations.
 Experience leading regulatory compliance programs in a highly regulated environment.
 Strong regulatory judgment and demonstrated ability to translate complex requirements into operational processes, controls, and clear ownership.
 Demonstrated experience strengthening or scaling compliance operations, including process documentation, business continuity, controls, and performance management.
 Experience working with government agencies, regulators, auditors, Legal, and cross-functional business partners.
 Demonstrated ability to identify and manage regulatory, operational, and business continuity risks.
 Strong people leadership, coaching, and performance management skills.
 Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate risks and priorities to senior leaders.
 Proven ability to influence and drive outcomes across functions.
 Preferred

title: QA Associate II
description:
The QA Associate II is responsible for ensuring the accurate, compliant, and timely release of Twist's synthetic biology products, with a primary focus on batch record review, raw material and lot release, and quality event support. Working in an ISO 13485 manufacturing environment, this role partners closely with production, equipment, and subject matter experts to investigate quality events, support root cause analysis, and keep documentation and processes inspection-ready. A strong working knowledge of cGMP and IVD regulatory requirements, along with high attention to detail and clear communication, is critical to success in this role. This is a great opportunity for a quality professional who enjoys hands-on, on-site work and wants to grow their impact by mentoring peers and supporting internal and external audits.
 Knowledge & Application 
 Ensures the accurate and safe release of various synthetic biology products in accordance with company and/or client procedures and requirements.
 Ensures and promotes compliance with applicable ISO, cGMP, IVD Regulations, and company and client SOPs.
 Authors and reviews relevant SOPs, batch records, labels and other documents.
 Manufacturing Batch Record review, control, release, including label verification.
 Materials management (including Raw Material Release), nonconformance disposition and release activity as applicable.
 Collaborates with SMEs to investigate Quality event tickets and assign, approve, or follow up on approval and disposition of these events.
 Review and releases IQOQPQs through collaboration with the Equipment team.
 Support the tracking and trending relevant quality metrics as assigned.
 Support investigations, root cause analysis, and documentation of findings on Quality Events.
 Conduct lab walkthroughs on a periodic basis and report and follow up on findings.
 Effectively influences (by serving as a peer mentor) and trains employees on basic releases and processes.
 Supports internal and external audits via gathering and preparation of audit material.
 Support additional responsibilities as assigned.
 Ability to be on-site to inspect products/materials and release lots.
 Follow regulatory and ISO 13485 requirements.
 Complexity & Problem Solving 
 Executes tasks/assignments that have clear and established processes and procedures. At times, tasks/assignments require occasional adaptation beyond established processes and procedures.
 Collaboration & Interaction 
 Follows established procedures on routine work, receives instructions only on new assignments.
 Typical Degree & Years of Experience 
 Bachelors degree (or equivalent) in a scientific /engineering related field
 2-3 years of experience in the medical device/pharmaceutical/biotech industry.
 Minimum 2 years of Quality Assurance or Regulatory Compliance (e.g. GCP, cGMP, GLP) experience.
 Experience working and/or supporting production/laboratories a plus.
 Familiarity with regulatory requirements for IVD Products, ISO 13485, 21CFR820, MDD, applicable experience in medical device, or biotech manufacturing and a thorough knowledge and understanding of cGMP.
 Familiarity with Confluence and JIRA applications desired.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills.
 Analytical and problem-solving skills.
 Proven ability to work cross-functionally to achieve business outcomes.

title: Associate Director, HEOR & Market Access, EU West
description:
Mavericks Wanted 
 When was the last time you achieved the impossible? If that thought feels overwhelming, you might want to pause here, but if it sparks excitement...read on 
 In 2015, we pioneered a “moneyball for biotech” approach, pooling projects and promising early-stage research from academia together under one financial umbrella to reduce risk and unleash innovation. This model allows science and small teams of experts to lead the way. We build bridges to groundbreaking advancements in rare disease, and develop life-changing medicines for patients with unmet needs as fast as humanly possible. 
 Together we define white space, push boundaries, and empower people to solve problems. If you're someone who defies convention, join us and work alongside some of the most respected minds in the industry. Together, we'll ask "why not?" and help reengineer the future of biopharma. At BridgeBio, we value curiosity and experimentation-including the ethical & thoughtful use of AI to improve clarity, speed, and quality of work. 
 What You'll Do 
 You will report to the Senior Director, Head of Market Access, EU West Region and work closely with Medical affairs, Market Access, Commercial locally and globally, to support BridgeBio's mission of delivering transformative medicines to patients with genetic rare diseases.
 You will own the value demonstration strategy for our products across the region, and translate it into effective patient access: design each product's evidence generation plan, drive it through to delivery, and align it with pricing and access strategy, starting in France, then extending to the other countries of the EU West region
 Your main responsibilities include:
 Evidence generation 
 Design and lead natural history studies, cohorts, registries, and analyses of medico-administrative databases (SNDS, BNDMR/ BaMaRa, rare disease network registries)
 Lead indirect comparisons in the context of single-arm trials and very small patient populations
 Develop health economic models (cost-effectiveness, budget impact) for France, then for other markets in the region
 Design real-world data collection frameworks (PUT-RD / data collection protocols) that can be reused for reassessment and in other countries
 Define the scientific publication and communication plan
 Study management 
 Draft specifications, run tenders, and select vendors
 Convene and lead external scientific advisory committees
 Secure all required approvals (health data access, ethics committees, regulatory compliance)
 Manage the administrative, contractual, and budgetary aspects of studies
 Review and validate all deliverables (protocols, analysis plans, study reports, publications)
 Value communication and internal expertise 
 Translate study results into actionable clinical and economic arguments
 Drive scientific dissemination (congresses, publications)
 Serve as the internal reference point on epidemiology, health economics, and health data matters
 Build and maintain a network of research agencies, academics, and institutions
 Value and access strategy 
 Define and own the value demonstration strategy for each product across the region
 Build economic value propositions and value dossiers and ensure their local adaptation
 Contribute to pricing strategy and preparation for CEPS negotiations (e.g., positive externalities, budget impact)
 Coordinate and build the economic modelling and CEESP dossier (early scientific advice, modelling, CEESP submission, technical exchange, etc.)
 Contribute the health-economic and RWE content of early access dossiers and submissions to the Transparency Committee, in coordination with the Market Access Director, with progressively increasing ownership of Benelux dossiers
 Anticipate assessors' objections and build responses ahead of submission
 French rare disease ecosystem 
 Build working relationships with rare disease networks, reference and competence centres, patient associations, and learned societies
 Negotiate collaborations with existing registries and cohorts
 Contribute to documenting the patient journey and disease burden
 Function leadership and development 
 Own and arbitrate the region's HEOR and RWE budget
 Structure the function (methods, quality standards, vendor panel, review processes)
 Recruit and manage future team members
 Represent the region to global HEOR and Market Access teams
 The above list of tasks is not exhaustive.
 Where You'll Work 
 This is a France-based role
 Travel within France, a priority country, is expected, as is travel to our international office in Zug, Switzerland, for team alignment and engagement.
 Travel to other countries in the EU West region may also be required. Local team meetings and the designated office location in France are in the Paris area.
 Who You Are 
 7-10 years of experience in HEOR, real-world evidence (RWE), or market access within industry, biotech, or specialized consulting
 Direct, hands-on experience completing French market access dossiers, including submissions to the Transparency Committee, early access applications, and CEESP assessments
 Strong knowledge of observational studies, medico-administrative databases, health economic modeling, and indirect comparisons
 Proven experience managing vendors and budgets
 Ability to influence without direct authority and collaborate with global, multidisciplinary teams
 A background in pharmacy, medicine, epidemiology, health economics, or biostatistics, with a master's or doctoral degree
 Fluency in French and professional proficiency in English
 Strongly preferred 
 Experienced in rare or ultra-rare diseases
 Experienced defending a surrogate endpoint or biomarker
 Knowledge of French rare disease networks
 Exposure to Belgian, Dutch, or Central and Eastern European systems
 Initial people management experience
 Experience in biotech or a fast-growing organization
 Expected attributes 
 Quickly operate independently, with a strong sense of ownership
 Ability to prioritize across multiple geographies
 Critical thinking and methodological rigor
 Compelling communication in both French and English
 Directness and clarity in all exchanges
 As a global company, our comprehensive benefits may vary based on location. We have high expectations for our team members. We make sure those working hard for patients are rewarded and cared for in return. 
 For BridgeBio Full-Time U.S Based Roles: 
 Financial & Rewards 
 Market-leading compensation 
 401(k) with employer match 
 Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP) 
 Pre-tax commuter benefits (transit and parking) 
 Referral bonus for hired candidates 
 Subsidized lunch and parking on in-office days 
 Health & Well-Being 
 100% employer-paid medical, dental, and vision premiums for you and your dependents 
 Health Savings Account (HSA) with annual employer contributions, plus Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) 
 Fertility & family-forming benefits 
 Expanded mental health support (therapy and coaching resources) 
 Hybrid work model with flexibility 
 Flexible, “take-what-you-need” paid time off and company-paid holidays 
 Comprehensive paid medical and parental leave to care for yourself and your family 
 Skill Development & Career Paths: 
 People are part of our growth and success story - from discovery to active drug trials and FDA pipelines, there are endless opportunities for skill development and internal mobility 
 We provide career pathing through regular feedback, continuous education and professional development programs via LinkedIn Learning, LifeLabs, & BetterUp Coaching 
 We celebrate strong performance with financial rewards, peer-to-peer recognition, and growth opportunities 
 By applying, you acknowledge that BridgeBio will process your personal information as described in our Global Candidate Privacy Notice . Questions or requests: dataprivacy@bridgebio.com

title: Principal Customer Success Manager - Pharma
description:
At H1 , we believe access to the best healthcare information is a basic human right. Our mission is to provide a platform that can optimally inform every doctor interaction globally. This promotes health equity and builds needed trust in healthcare systems. To accomplish this our teams harness the power of data and AI-technology to unlock groundbreaking medical insights and convert those insights into action that result in optimal patient outcomes and accelerates an equitable and inclusive drug development lifecycle. Visit h1.co to learn more about us.
 H1's Customer Success team is focused on building deep, trusted relationships with existing customers to ensure they successfully implement the H1 platform, drive sustained engagement, and realize measurable business value from our solutions.
 WHAT YOU'LL DO AT H1 
The primary objective of the Principal Customer Success Manager is to serve as a strategic, trusted advisor to a portfolio of H1's largest and most complex customers. You will own the customer relationship end-to-end, partnering closely with both senior client stakeholders and users to drive adoption, value realization, retention, and growth across either H1's Clinical or Medical & Commercial product lines.
 This role is designed for a highly autonomous, principal-level Customer Success leader who thrives in ambiguity, independently owns complex customer programs, strong personal accountability, and influences outcomes across customers, partners, and internal teams. Success in this role requires exceptional judgment, executive presence, and the ability to lead without direct authority.
 You will:
- Own large-scale customer programs involving multiple business units, internal teams, System Integrators (SIs), and executive stakeholders.
- Lead cross-functional initiatives by establishing governance, driving accountability, managing dependencies, and ensuring successful execution across internal and external teams.
- Operate as the strategic point of contact for complex customer engagements, aligning competing priorities while driving measurable business outcomes and managing the overall account.
- Lead multiple concurrent, cross-functional customer programs, balancing competing priorities across customer executives, implementation partners, and internal stakeholders while maintaining alignment on strategic objectives.
- Build strong relationships with senior and executive-level stakeholders, positioning H1 as a critical partner in achieving their organizational goals.
- Operate with minimal oversight while independently prioritizing competing customer and business needs.
- Exercise sound judgment in highly ambiguous situations where there may not be an established playbook.
- Identify gaps, define solutions, and drive execution without requiring direction from leadership.
- Successfully navigate complex stakeholder dynamics during periods of organizational change or customer escalation.
- Own and drive account strategy, including implementation and adoption plans, success metrics, renewal readiness, and expansion opportunities.
- Lead regular executive business reviews, clearly articulating performance against KPIs, ROI, and strategic impact.
- Serve as the voice of the customer internally, providing structured feedback to product, engineering, and leadership teams to inform roadmap and prioritization.
- Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Sales, and Support to ensure a seamless customer experience across the full lifecycle.
- Consistently drive improvements in MAUs, NPS, CSAT, retention, and ARR across your book of business.
- Proactively identify and mitigate risk across all areas of the account.
 ABOUT YOU 
We're looking for a Principal Customer Success Manager who is passionate about delivering measurable value to enterprise customers at scale. You bring a strategic mindset, strong executive presence, and the ability to balance deep problem-solving with long-term relationship management. You thrive in fast-paced environments and take pride in owning outcomes for your customers.
- You quickly establish credibility and require little ramp-up to begin managing strategic customer relationships in the Pharma & CRO space.
- You naturally create structure in ambiguous environments and enjoy solving complex organizational challenges.
- You have exceptional ownership and accountability, following through on commitments without requiring close oversight.
- You are known for bringing order to difficult customer situations and driving successful outcomes.
- You influence without authority and effectively lead cross-functional teams toward shared objectives.
 REQUIREMENTS 
- 5+ years of experience in Customer Success, Account Management, Consulting, Program Management, or equivalent strategic customer-facing experience within an Enterprise or Strategic B2B SaaS environment.
- Demonstrated experience owning complex, high-ARR accounts with senior stakeholder engagement.
- Strong project management experience across multi-threaded, high-priority initiatives.
- Experience working in or with Life Sciences organizations strongly preferred; Medical Affairs or Clinical experience is a plus.
- Proven ability to manage renewals, mitigate risk, and identify expansion opportunities.
 COMPENSATION 
This role pays $145,000 to $160,000 per year, based on experience, plus variable commission, based on performance, in addition to stock options.
 Anticipated role close date: 09/21/2026
 Compensation
 Additional Information
 H1 OFFERS 
 - Full suite of health insurance options, in addition to generous paid time off
 - Pre-planned company-wide wellness holidays
 - Retirement options
 - Health & charitable donation stipends
 - Impactful Business Resource Groups
 - Flexible work hours & the opportunity to work from anywhere
 - The opportunity to work with leading biotech and life sciences companies in an innovative industry with a mission to improve healthcare around the globe
 H1 is proud to be an equal opportunity employer that celebrates diversity and is committed to creating an inclusive workplace with equal opportunity for all applicants and teammates. Our goal is to recruit the most talented people from a diverse candidate pool regardless of race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, disability, sex (including pregnancy), age, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. 
 H1 is committed to working with and providing access and reasonable accommodation to applicants with mental and/or physical disabilities. If you require an accommodation, please reach out to your recruiter once you've begun the interview process. All requests for accommodations are treated discreetly and confidentially, as practical and permitted by law.

title: Phone Numbers Operations Specialist 1
description:
Who we are 
 At Twilio, we're shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes. We deliver innovative solutions to hundreds of thousands of businesses and empower millions of developers worldwide to craft personalized customer experiences.
 Our dedication to remote-first work , and strong culture of connection and global inclusion means that no matter your location, you're part of a vibrant team with diverse experiences making a global impact each day. As we continue to revolutionize how the world interacts, we're acquiring new skills and experiences that make work feel truly rewarding. Your career at Twilio is in your hands.
 . 
 Hiring and how we work 
 We use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Twilions! 
 Also, while we are a remote-first company, you may be asked to report in person on an ad-hoc basis for team gatherings, functional off-sites or customer meetings. 
 . 
 See yourself at Twilio 
 Join the team as Twilio's next Product Operation Specialist 1.
 About the job 
 Twilio is seeking a Product Operations Specialist I to support our Porting and Hosting Operations-a key component of Twilio's Global Number Management team. This role ensures customers can seamlessly port phone numbers, manage number hosting, and experience reliable service during transitions. You'll work across carrier networks, internal tools, and product teams to troubleshoot, coordinate, and optimize porting workflows at scale.
 The Level 1 role is an entry-level position ideal for someone who is detail-oriented, process-driven, with excelsior customer servicing skills and excited to work at the intersection of product, operations, and telecom. This position plays a vital role in ensuring Twilio's phone number experience remains best-in-class.
 Responsibilities 
 In this role, you'll:
 Wear the Customer's Shoes : Champion the customer experience by managing inbound porting requests with care, urgency, and accuracy. Ensure customers have a seamless transition when bringing their phone numbers to Twilio or managing hosted services.
 Be Inclusive : Collaborate with a diverse team of engineers, support agents, product managers, and carrier partners. Respect different communication styles, cultures, and perspectives while driving unified outcomes.
 Empower Others : Proactively share insights, documentation, and solutions with peers and partner teams to make operational processes easier and more transparent. Help elevate the broader team by contributing to best practices.
 Write It Down : Maintain accurate records of porting workflows, number hosting cases, escalations, and system usage. Keep internal knowledge bases and documentation up to date to ensure reliability and consistency across teams.
 No Shenanigans : Follow industry and regulatory standards in number portability and telecom compliance. Protect customer data and make ethical decisions when managing sensitive porting and routing scenarios.
 Be Bold : Take initiative in solving problems and navigating complexity, even when documentation is limited. Don't hesitate to raise questions, propose improvements, or flag issues that impact the customer experience.
 Draw the Owl : Identify recurring issues and inefficiencies in porting and hosting operations. Use your findings to improve workflows, tooling, or automation - even when there's no clear roadmap.
 Don't Settle : Aim to exceed SLAs and continuously look for ways to optimize how we execute core operations. Be relentless about quality, efficiency, and learning from mistakes.
 Qualifications 
 Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!
 *Required: 
 2 years of experience in BPO, customer campaigns, tech support, customer operations, product operations, customer service, QA or other related areas of customer service like inventory, finance, quality operations, customer support, customer or team training.
 Bilingual: Spanish and English proficiency 
 Strong organizational skills and ability to manage detailed processes with accuracy.
 Basic data analysis (Excel/Google Sheets, SQL), or automation tools.
 Structured thinking.
 Basic AI prompting and workflow building.
 Excellent verbal and written communication, both internally and with external partners.
 Comfort working with tools like ticketing systems (Excel, Zendesk, JIRA), spreadsheets, and internal platforms.
 Able to learn quickly, adapt to changing processes, and work independently while collaborating cross-functionally.
 Customer-centric mindset with strong attention to detail and a proactive attitude.
 Desired: 
 Experience with telecom Industry
 Exposure to APIs.
 Location 
 This role will be remote, and based in Colombia.
 Travel 
 We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, you may be required to travel occasionally to participate in project or team in-person meetings.
 What We Offer 
 Working at Twilio offers many benefits, including competitive pay, generous time off, ample parental and wellness leave, healthcare, a retirement savings program, and much more. Offerings vary by location.
 Twilio thinks big. Do you? 
 We like to solve problems, take initiative, pitch in when needed, and are always up for trying new things. That's why we seek out colleagues who embody our values - something we call Twilio Magic . Additionally, we empower employees to build positive change in their communities by supporting their volunteering and donation efforts.
 So, if you're ready to unleash your full potential, do your best work, and be the best version of yourself, apply now! If this role isn't what you're looking for, please consider other open positions. 
 . 
 Stay alert to recruitment fraud 
 We care about your safety. Scammers sometimes impersonate Twilio recruiters through fake job postings, emails, websites, or messages. Please ensure you are engaging with an official @ twilio.com email address. We will never ask for payment, gift cards, cryptocurrency, or banking information during the recruiting process. We do not make job offers without a formal interview process or conduct interviews exclusively through text-based messaging apps.
 . 
 Twilio is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, reproductive health decisions, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, political views or activity, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act. Additionally, Twilio participates in the E-Verify program in certain locations, as required by law.

title: Supply Chain Program Manager: Inbound
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE
Hinge Health is seeking a highly skilled Supply Chain Program Manager to join the company's Logistics team. As the Supply Chain Program Manager, Inbound, you will own the end-to-end inbound process for international products, partnering with vendors, our customs broker, logistics, and cross-functional hardware teams to keep inbound operations running smoothly.
This role is ideal for an experienced supply chain or operations program manager who enjoys solving practical problems, improving established processes, and seeing the direct impact of their work. You will manage vendor-facing programs, customs and duty workflows, commercial documentation, and invoice validation while helping Hinge Health deliver products to members on time.
WHAT YOU'LL ACCOMPLISH
IN YOUR FIRST 3 MONTHS
 - Take ownership of the existing inbound process and establish clear operating rhythms, responsibilities, and escalation paths.
 - Build strong working relationships with international vendors, the customs broker, logistics partners, and Hardware Operations stakeholders.
 - Review inbound product flows, customs and duty requirements, HS-code usage, commercial documentation, and invoice-validation practices.
 - Identify the highest-impact process gaps and risks affecting product timing, cost, documentation quality, or vendor execution.
 - Establish regular reporting on inbound status, exceptions, documentation issues, and actions required to keep products moving.
IN YOUR FIRST 6 MONTHS
 - Manage the end-to-end inbound process for international products, from vendor coordination through customs clearance, receipt, and invoice validation.
 - Coordinate with vendors and the customs broker to resolve documentation, classification, duty, and clearance issues.
 - Ensure required commercial documents include accurate and relevant information, including appropriate HS codes and supporting details.
 - Validate invoices against agreed pricing, shipment information, and supporting documentation, escalating discrepancies to the appropriate stakeholders.
 - Partner with logistics and Hardware Operations to improve inbound handoffs, reduce avoidable delays, and maintain reliable product flow.
 - Track vendor performance and recurring operational issues, then drive practical corrective actions with internal and external partners.
IN YOUR FIRST YEAR
 - Enhance the scalability, consistency, and visibility of Hinge Health's inbound operating process as product and vendor needs evolve.
 - Develop and maintain clear process documentation, operating procedures, and controls for inbound execution, customs and duties, and invoice validation.
 - Identify opportunities to reduce cost, improve vendor performance, and increase predictability across the inbound supply chain.
 - Lead cross-functional initiatives that strengthen supply chain operations and support new product or hardware programs.
 - Travel locally to vendors when needed to strengthen partnerships, understand operational constraints, and resolve issues at the source.
WHO YOU ARE
 - You are an experienced supply chain or operations program manager who can manage complex, vendor-facing processes from end to end.
 - You are comfortable working across international inbound operations, customs and duties, commercial documentation, and invoice validation.
 - You are a practical problem solver who can move between strategic process improvement and detailed day-to-day execution.
 - You build trust with vendors and internal partners, communicate clearly, and drive accountability without relying on formal authority.
 - You take ownership of outcomes, follow issues through to resolution, and use data and operating details to make sound decisions.
 - You are energized by visible impact and enjoy improving real-world systems rather than working only at a theoretical or reporting level.
BASIC QUALIFICATIONS
 - 5+ years of experience in supply chain, operations, or program management, including experience managing international inbound products and vendors.
 - Working knowledge of customs and duties processes, including the use of HS codes and supporting commercial documentation.

title: Senior Commercial Lines Account Manager
description:
About Gusto 
 At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff - payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR - so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.
 All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) - because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy .
 AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.
 About the Role: 
 Gusto is building its own P&C insurance agency - moving from a third-party referral model to a first-party, payroll-integrated experience that protects small businesses as they grow. We have policies in force and a growing book of business. What we don't yet have is a licensed account manager inside the company servicing it. You'll be our first, and the foundation of the service function: owning daily servicing of the book, running the proactive outreach that keeps clients correctly covered, and turning every recurring case into a product spec so the next hundred don't need a human.
 About the Team: 
 The Business Insurance team is building Gusto's P&C insurance agency from the ground up, across core small commercial lines including Workers' Compensation. We partner closely with carrier counterparts and work hand-in-hand with product, engineering, design, data, sales, and licensed insurance professionals to ship a quote, bind, and service experience that's fast, accurate, and easy to manage over time. The team is small, cross-functional, and highly execution-oriented - ideal for someone who thrives in ambiguity and wants to build durable operations in a zero-to-one environment.
 Here's what you'll do day-to-day: 
 Own daily servicing of the assigned book: endorsements, certificates of insurance, coverage questions, premium audits, billing disputes, cancellations, reinstatements, and renewals.
 Accountable for outcomes connected to Business Insurance customers. 
 Serve as the liaison between insureds, carriers, and our licensed producers - explaining coverage, exclusions, and exposures in plain language.
 Run proactive outreach using payroll data a traditional agency doesn't have: catching FEIN mismatches, new-state hires, and class code drift before they become coverage gaps.
 Work the pending cancellation and non-pay queue - find out what's actually driving each cancellation, fix what's fixable, and secure reinstatement or replacement coverage.
 Handle claims intake and status reporting, and coordinate hand-offs to the carrier's adjusting team.
 Document every recurring case as a product spec, partnering with product and engineering to automate certificate generation, endorsement submission, and intake triage - using AI tools daily for drafting, summarization, and triage.
 Write the SOPs, escalation paths, and service standards for the team
 Here's what we're looking for: 
 5+ years of commercial lines service experience at an independent agency, brokerage, or carrier, servicing small commercial accounts end to end.
 Workers' Compensation depth - class codes, experience modifiers, premium audits, and state-specific requirements. Pay-as-you-go WC experience is a strong plus.
 Experience working in carrier portals (Hartford, AmTrust, etc) and coordinating with carrier underwriting/servicing teams to service an agency book of business. 
 AI and automation fluency - you've used AI tools in real service work (drafting, summarization, triage, outreach) and have opinions about where they hold up and where they don't.
 Evidence you build, not just execute - a process you documented, a workflow you redesigned, or a tool you got built. We'll ask for specifics.
 A compliance instinct: you know when something needs a licensed person, a carrier's sign-off, or a documented file, and you don't improvise around it.
 An active Property & Casualty producer license (Colorado resident preferred), or willingness to obtain one within 90 days of starting - we sponsor the coursework and exams - plus willingness to obtain nonresident licenses across our footprint over time.
 Preferred: industry designations (CISR, CIC, AAI, ACSR, or CPCU); multi-state or nonresident licensing already in place; experience at a digital agency, insurtech, or MGA, or having stood up a service function from scratch.
 If you don't think you meet every point above but you're excited about this work, apply anyway.
 Our cash compensation amount for this role is between $83,265 - $102,000/year in Denver. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate location, experience and expertise and may vary from the amounts listed above.
 At Gusto, we don't use titles the traditional way, as a signal of rank or hierarchy. Instead, our titles describe two things at once - your craft (what you do, e.g. Engineering, Design) and your scope of ownership (what you're accountable for) - which is why you'll see something like "Head of X" instead of a rank word like "Director" that tells you neither. Because of this, the title on this posting may look different from what you'd expect based on the scope and seniority of the role, and from how similar roles are typically titled elsewhere. If you have questions about how this role compares to your current title or level, your recruiter can help translate.
 Gusto has physical office spaces in Denver, San Francisco, and New York City. Employees who are based in those locations will be expected to work from the office on designated days approximately 2-3 days per week (or more depending on role). The same office expectations apply to all Symmetry roles, Gusto's subsidiary, whose physical office is in Scottsdale.
 Note: The San Francisco office expectations encompass both the San Francisco and San Jose metro areas. 
 When approved to work from a location other than a Gusto office, a secure, reliable, and consistent internet connection is required. This includes non-office days for hybrid employees.
 Reliable, consistent presence: We expect regular and predictable attendance, whether you're working in-office, hybrid, or fully remote, so that you stay closely connected to your team, customers, and stakeholders in real time and ensure colleagues and customers receive the timely support and responsiveness they deserve.
 Our customers come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds, not just because it's the right thing to do, but because it makes our company stronger. If you share our values and our enthusiasm for small businesses, you will find a home at Gusto. 
 Gusto is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in hiring or any employment decision based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, genetic information, veteran status, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. Gusto considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Gusto is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. We want to see our candidates perform to the best of their ability. If you require a medical or religious accommodation at any time throughout your candidate journey, please fill out this form and a member of our team will get in touch with you. 
 Gusto takes security and protection of your personal information very seriously. Please review our Fraudulent Activity Disclaimer .
 Personal information collected and processed as part of your Gusto application will be subject to Gusto's Applicant Privacy Notice .

title: Healthcare Account Manager
description:
At Qualtrics, we create software the world's best brands use to deliver exceptional frontline experiences, build high-performing teams, and design products people love. But we are more than a platform-we are the creators and stewards of the Experience Management category serving over 18K clients globally. Building a category takes grit, determination, and a disdain for convention-but most of all it requires close-knit, high-functioning teams with an unwavering dedication to serving our customers. 
When you join one of our teams, you'll be part of a nimble group that's empowered to set aggressive goals and move fast to achieve them. Strategic risks are encouraged and complex problems are solved together, by passing the mic and iterating until the best solution comes to light. You won't have to look to find growth opportunities-ready or not, they'll find you. From retail to government to healthcare, we're on a mission to bring humanity, connection, and empathy back to business. Join over 5,000 people across the globe who think that's work worth doing.
 Healthcare Account Manager 
 Why We Have This Role 
 We're looking for an Account Executive to build deep, strategic relationships with healthcare providers and help them expand how they use the Qualtrics Experience Management SaaS platform. This account management role focuses on growing existing customer accounts, rather than prospecting for new logos. You'll dig beneath surface answers to understand each customer's healthcare priorities, build a strategy around their program, and connect their needs with the right solutions across our suites.
You'll work with a range of stakeholders, from CEOs and chief nursing officers to quality, HR, and marketing leaders and frontline staff. Success means understanding their different priorities and showing how our solutions can help address the problems they face in their day-to-day work. This role is based in Dallas with a hybrid working arrangement.
 How You'll Find Success 
 Stay curious and coachable, asking questions to understand customers' needs and deepen your healthcare and product knowledge.
 Balance long-term relationship-building with identifying growth and expansion opportunities within an existing book of accounts.
 Understand how healthcare organizations operate, including their quality and safety priorities, decision-making structures, and the needs of different stakeholders.
 Communicate confidently with executives, clinical leaders, quality directors, HR and marketing teams, and frontline staff.
 Stay highly organized while managing a large portfolio and competing customer priorities.
 How You'll Grow 
 Clear, structured promotion path via Qualtrics' auto-promotion framework and continuous Career Action Planning with your manager.
 Access to internal mobility platform Qmobility for additional growth opportunities.
 Skill development in business acumen, complex negotiation, and consultative selling.
 Opportunity to expand your healthcare expertise and deepen partnerships across strategic accounts.
 Things You'll Do 
 Build and grow relationships with existing healthcare provider customers, taking a long-term, relationship-based approach to selling.
 Develop account strategies that identify customer needs and opportunities to expand into additional solutions.
 Lead discovery conversations, listen closely to customers' challenges, and position products that address those needs.
 Navigate complex sales involving multiple buyers and stakeholders across a healthcare organization.
 Deliver product demonstrations and explain the value of our solutions to both executive and operational audiences.
 Manage a large book of business, stay organized across competing priorities, and maintain momentum across multiple customer relationships.
 What We're Looking For On Your Resume 
 5+ years of sales experience, including 2+ years in a closing role, with evidence of growing and developing customer accounts.
 A working understanding of healthcare and the ability to navigate healthcare provider organizations, including conversations about quality, safety, and operational priorities.
 Experience navigating complex sales with multiple stakeholders and adapting your approach to different audiences.
 A consultative, problem-solving approach: you can connect what a customer needs with an appropriate solution rather than lead with a product pitch.
 Strong organization and prioritization skills for managing a large portfolio of accounts.
 Experience selling multiple products, a solution suite, or a platform is helpful. Your background does not need to be exclusively in SaaS or technology sales; what matters is your ability to navigate healthcare, manage complex sales, and build lasting customer relationships.
 What You Should Know About This Team 
 A healthcare provider account management team focused on long-term relationships and customer expansion, rather than new-logo hunting.
 Work that spans multiple solution sets and a wide range of stakeholders within each customer organization.
 An emphasis on understanding healthcare customers' problems and showing how the right solution can address them.
 Our Team's Favorite Perks and Benefits 
 Competitive salary plus uncapped commissions and accelerators rewarding outstanding performance.
 100% merit-based promotions, driven by results and impact rather than politics or tenure.
 Flexible hybrid work environment supporting jeans and dogs in the office.
 Catered lunches, quarterly team socials, winter and summer parties, and extensive Qualtrics swag.
 Private health insurance, annual Qualtrics Experience Bonus, wellness stipend to support your personal well-being and growth.
 The Qualtrics Hybrid Work Model : Our hybrid work model is elegantly simple: we all gather in the office three days a week; Mondays and Thursdays, plus one day selected by your organizational leader. These purposeful in-person days in thoughtfully designed offices help us do our best work and harness the power of collaboration and innovation. For the rest of the week, work where you want, owning the integration of work and life. #hybrid

title: Operations Manager, Product Implementation
description:
About Lyra Health
Lyra Health is a leading provider of evidence-based mental health care, serving more than 20 million people globally in partnership with employers and more than 100 million through health plan and partner relationships. The company has delivered more than 15 million sessions of mental health care, published more than 35 peer-reviewed studies, and delivered unmatched outcomes in terms of access, clinical effectiveness, and cost efficiency. Extensive peer-reviewed research confirms Lyra's transformative care model helps people recover twice as fast and results in a 26% annual reduction in overall healthcare claims costs. Lyra is transforming access to life-changing mental health care through Lyra Empower, the only fully integrated, AI-powered platform combining the highest-quality care and technology solutions. 
About The Role
We are seeking a strategic Operations Manager to join our Provider Core Ops Systems Implementation team. In this role, you will lead and scale our Systems Architecture team, driving the operational strategy and multi-system integrations that power Lyra's provider network platform. You will serve as the bridge between business strategy and technical execution, partnering directly with Product, Engineering, Clinical, and Operations leaders to solve complex infrastructure challenges and ensure seamless, sustainable data flows across provider-facing systems.
Core Focus Areas
Team Leadership: Lead, mentor, and empower a high-performing team of Systems Architecture leads and individual contributors.
Architectural Ownership: Independently own complex cross-system integrations and multi-tool data pipelines across Workday, Salesforce, and downstream platforms.
Cross-Functional Alignment: Translate Clinical and Operations strategy into actionable technical roadmaps while resolving cross-departmental bottlenecks.
Responsibilities: People Management & Team Leadership: Serve as direct people manager to the Product Implementation pillar within Provider Core Ops. Develop tactical team plans, delegate effectively, and invest in team culture, performance, and career development.
 End-to-End Product Implementation: Own the operational strategy and execution of product and policy changes across the full product lifecycle. Ensure internal provider and external client/partner audiences are enabled for success.
 Cross-Functional Strategic Unblocking: Act as the primary operational liaison to Product, Tech, and Clinical leadership. Poke holes early in product development, surface risk, reconcile program goals with macro business goals, and align competing stakeholder priorities.
 Playbook Development & Continuous Improvement: Evolve and maintain standardized product development and launch playbooks to support rapid platform growth across diverse service lines and provider network structures.
 Systems & Product Synergy: Work in tandem with the Systems Architecture pillar to ensure user-facing product features map seamlessly to underlying data infrastructure.
 Change Management & Strategic Communications: Oversee implementation comms and enablement strategies to ensure providers and clinical ops teams navigate platform shifts smoothly and feel supported in delivering care.
Qualifications: Experience: 8+ years of professional experience in Product Operations, Clinical Operations, Program Management, Business Operations, or a related high-growth digital health/healthcare function.
 People Leadership: Proven track record as a direct people manager with demonstrated success setting operational roadmaps, delegating effectively, managing senior ICs, and mentoring team members.
 Product & Systems Acumen: Deep experience navigating the software development lifecycle, product rollouts, and tech stacks (Salesforce, EHR, Zendesk, Asana, Jira).
 Healthcare & Clinical Context: Direct experience working closely with clinicians, care providers, or clinical leadership in a healthcare or digital health setting; deep understanding of how to balance clinical workflows with product growth goals.
 Strategic Communication & XFN Influence: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; proven ability to storytell, manage senior executive/XFN stakeholders, and negotiate competing priorities across departments.
 Operational Insight: Strong analytical acumen and fluency with operational and product health metrics to evaluate launch success, measure adoption, and continuously refine processes.

title: Associate QA Engineer
description:
Veeva Systems is a mission-driven organization and pioneer in industry cloud, helping life sciences companies bring therapies to patients faster. As one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies in history, we surpassed $3B in revenue in our last fiscal year with extensive growth potential ahead.
At the heart of Veeva are our values: Do the Right Thing, Customer Success, Employee Success, and Speed. We're not just any public company - we made history in 2021 by becoming a public benefit corporation (PBC), legally bound to balancing the interests of customers, employees, society, and investors.
As a Work Anywhere company, we support your flexibility to work from home or in the office, so you can thrive in your ideal environment.
Join us in transforming the life sciences industry, committed to making a positive impact on its customers, employees, and communities.
The Role
Nitro is an AI-native data platform that democratizes life sciences data for non-technical commercial teams, turning fragmented HCP/HCO, prescription, and industry data into decisions the field can act on. We're looking for a QA Engineer to drive quality for the platform and help modernize how we test it. Here, testing isn't a gate bolted onto the end of shipping, it's part of the same function as building and deploying. You'll own your share of that full chain. This is a junior role for someone who wants to build a real career in QA and automation. You'll start hands-on with day-to-day testing and grow into broader ownership of our test automation as you develop. We're investing in making our testing environment more AI-forward, and you'll have real room to shape and extend that work, not just maintain what exists. The function itself is evolving, too: our Operations org is moving from traditional QA toward evaluating AI-native systems, and this role is your entry point into where that's headed. 
What You'll Do Own day-to-day QA across releases: new data connectors, schema changes, customer rollouts, platform upgrades, ensuring changes are solid before they reach customers 
 Help cut down false-failure noise in the test suite and improve how efficiently it runs, so the team can trust what it's telling them 
 Get close enough to the business logic behind our data pipelines to know not just whether a test passes, but whether it's testing the right thing 
 Build new automations as new features roll out
