title: Lead Operations Associate, Customer Experience
description:
About Upstart 
 At Upstart, we're united by a mission that matters: to radically reduce the cost and complexity of borrowing for all Americans. Every day, we bring creativity, experimentation, and advanced AI to reshape access to credit, helping millions move forward financially with clarity and confidence.
 As the leading AI lending marketplace, we partner with banks and credit unions to expand access to affordable credit through technology that's both radically intelligent and deeply human. Our platform runs over one million predictions per borrower using more than 3,000 signals, powering smarter, fairer decisions for millions of customers. But the numbers only hint at the impact. Every idea, every voice, and every contribution moves us closer to a world where credit never stands between people and their financial progress.
 We're proudly digital-first, giving most Upstarters the flexibility to do their best work from wherever they thrive, alongside teammates across 80+ cities in the US and Canada. Digital-first doesn't mean distant. We're intentional about in-person connection through team onsites, planning sessions, and moments that spark creativity and trust. And whether you choose to work primarily from home or collaborate in-person from one of our offices in Columbus, Austin, the Bay Area, or New York City, you'll have the support to work in the way that works best for you.

 The Team: 
 Upstart's Customer Experience team helps applicants navigate the borrowing process across phone, email, and chat. The team combines customer support, operational expertise, and collaboration across departments to resolve issues accurately and improve the applicant experience.

 Improve performance across phone, email, and chat by monitoring queue health, service levels, backlog, and operational trends, and recommending timely responses to staffing gaps and bottlenecks.

 Experience resolving complex customer or operational issues across systems and customer support channels.

 Experience supporting peer development through training, process guidance, or routine feedback.
 Experience investigating root causes and coordinating operational improvements across teams, from gathering evidence through testing solutions and documenting outcomes.

 Consumer lending or fintech experience, including familiarity with verification, policy, or compliance workflows.
 Experience with workforce management platforms, routing systems, operational dashboards, or spreadsheet analysis.
 Experience building or improving AI tools, reusable prompt workflows, or operational automations, including testing outputs, evaluating results, and supporting adoption; experience with customer-facing AI or chatbot quality.
 Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain operational findings, influence without direct authority, and exercise judgment on sensitive escalations.
 Ability to manage competing priorities, adapt to feedback, and communicate risks with evidence and a recommended next step.

The majority of our employees can live and work anywhere in the U.S but are encouraged to to still spend high quality time in-person collaborating via regular onsites. The in-person sessions' cadence varies depending on the team and role; most teams meet once or twice per quarter for 2-4 consecutive days at a time.

 $28.56 - $39.52 USD

 At Upstart, our benefits for full-time employees are designed to support your health, financial well-being, family, and personal growth. Here's what you can expect:
 Competitive compensation, including base pay, bonus opportunities, and annual equity grants that vest quarterly

 Health Savings Account contributions from Upstart for eligible plans (US only)
 Income protection benefits, including life insurance and disability coverage for added financial security

 Family-centered benefits to support fertility, parenthood, and caregiving needs
 Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering mental health support and life-centered resources

 Annual wellness allowance to support your physical and emotional well-being and personal development, based on what matters most to you
 Annual productivity allowance to invest in relevant tools and resources you need to do your best work, no matter where you work from
 Connection and community through team events, all-company updates, and employee resource groups (ERGs)
 Onsite perks, including catered lunches and fully stocked micro-kitchens when working from one of our offices in the Bay Area, Austin, Columbus, and New York City

title: Staff Analyst, Analytics - Pharmacy Payment Integrity & Analytics
location: Charlotte, North Carolina, United States; Denver, Colorado, United States; New York, New York, United States
description:
About Judi Health 
 Judi Health is a health technology company providing benefit administration solutions to employers, unions, health plans, and government entities. Judi Health replaces fragmented, outdated systems with the industry's first Unified Claims ProcessingTM architecture, seamlessly consolidating pharmacy and medical benefit administration on a single, secure platform. By delivering true price transparency, eliminating unnecessary middleman fees, and leveraging advanced AI-powered care delivery, Judi Health helps clients achieve unprecedented operational efficiency and service levels.
At Judi Health, we're deploying the infrastructure our country needs to deliver the healthcare we all deserve. We are the intelligence platform powering benefits plans for millions of Americans and proudly leading the next generation of care. To learn more, visit www.judi.health .
 Location: Hybrid 3 days (offices in NYC, Denver, CO and Charlotte, NC area) 
 Position Summary: 
 We are seeking a highly analytical Analyst to join our Analytics team and support pharmacy claims integrity, adjudication validation, and operational excellence. This role will use SQL and large-scale pharmacy claims data to investigate claim outcomes, identify discrepancies, validate benefit and pricing configurations, and ensure claims adjudicate accurately and in accordance with contractual and regulatory requirements. 
 The ideal candidate combines strong analytical and technical skills with a natural curiosity for understanding how pharmacy claims are processed. They will work closely with Finance, Legal, Product, Operations, Network, and other cross-functional stakeholders to investigate issues, quantify impacts, support audits, and drive process improvements. This individual will play a key role in protecting financial accuracy, mitigating risk, and ensuring a high-quality member and pharmacy experience. 
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Analyze and Validate Pharmacy Claims 
 Use SQL and other analytical tools to review pharmacy claims data and validate adjudication outcomes. 
 I nvestigate claim pricing, benefit application, reimbursement calculations, accumulators, and other claim-processing logic to identify discrepancies or errors. 
 Perform root cause analyses on adjudication issues and partner with stakeholders to develop corrective actions. 
 Develop repeatable monitoring and surveillance processes to identify anomalies, trends, and potential financial or operational risks. 
 Partner Across Functional Teams 
 Collaborate with Finance, Legal, Product, Operations, Network, and Compliance teams to interpret requirements and assess claim-processing outcomes. 
 Support audits, regulatory reviews, contractual validations, and financial reconciliations through detailed claims analysis. 
 Translate technical findings into clear, actionable recommendations for business stakeholders. 
 Participate in cross-functional discussions to evaluate system changes, benefit implementations, and operational processes. 
 Deliver High-Quality Analytics 
 Develop and maintain SQL queries, reports, dashboards, and analytical tools that support claims oversight and operational decision-making. 
 Ensure analyses are accurate , well-documented, reproducible, and supported by appropriate quality controls. 
 I dentify opportunities for automation and process improvement to increase efficiency and reduce risk. 
 Support Risk Management and Compliance 
 Help identify and quantify financial, operational, and compliance risks associated with claims processing. 
 Validate that claims adjudicate in accordance with benefit designs, contractual requirements, and company policies. 
 Maintain documentation of methodologies, business rules, findings, and remediation activities. 
 Qualifications & Experience: 
 4-6 years of experience in healthcare analytics, pharmacy analytics, PBM operations, claims auditing, or a related field. 
 Advanced SQL skills with the ability to analyze large, complex datasets. 
 Experience performing pharmacy reimbursement, network pricing, financial reconciliation, contract compliance, or payment-integrity analysis. 
 Ability to interpret complex contractual pricing terms and convert them into documented calculations, validation rules, and analytical test cases. 
 Experience investigating discrepancies across claims, pricing reference data, contract terms, adjudication logic, and financial outputs. 
 Demonstrated ability to quantify financial exposure and communicate material findings, assumptions, and limitations to Finance, Legal, Network, Product, and executive stakeholders. 
 Preferred Qualifications: 
 PBM industry experience 
 Experience with pharmacy network contracting, reimbursement analysis, effective-rate reconciliation, or contract compliance 
 Experience using drug reference and pharmacy reference data 
 Familiarity with financial controls, audit support, accrual processes, recoveries, or materiality assessment 
 Experience creating automated exception monitoring and reconciliation frameworks

title: Manager, Account Manager | Growth
location: New York, NY (HQ); San Francisco, CA
description:
ABOUT RAMP
Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you've built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year - far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.
About The Role
The next chapter of Ramp's growth runs straight through the customers we already have: 80,000+ finance teams who adopted us for one thing and haven't yet seen what the rest of the platform can do for them. Account Management owns that opportunity - and this role owns the team building the motion to capture it.
You'll lead a group of 5-8 Account Managers, each carrying a book of ~3,000 emerging and SMB customers with real latitude over how they grow it. This is a build role, not a maintain role: the playbooks, coaching systems, and performance bar you set are the ones this team runs on next year. Your ceiling is set by how well you turn individual AM judgment into a repeatable, scalable motion that grows the segment.
What You'll Do
 - Build and run a high-performing team of 5-8 Account Managers - setting the bar for culture, morale, and daily execution.
 - Understand where to prioritize your teams time. Engage directly with AMs to identify and break into top accounts, especially where trust is being built or repaired.
 - Own the number. Manage quota performance and pipeline generation across your team to hit spend activation, product activation, retention, and expansion goals. Forecast your business to senior leadership on a weekly cadence.
 - Hire and develop the next generation of AMs - training on product, buyer personas, competition, and tooling through role-plays, game film, and real deal work.

title: Workplace Program Manager
description:
Toast creates technology to help restaurants and local businesses succeed in a digital world, helping business owners operate, increase sales, engage customers, and keep employees happy. 
 As the Workplace Program Manager, you will serve as the strategic "Product Owner" for our Americas workplace environments and operations. In this high-impact individual contributor role, you will define, scale, and run our regional workplace experience program while laying the operational foundation for long-term growth. This position is equal parts operator, program manager, and cultural champion. You will oversee our outsourced partner vendor model, establish core SLAs and KPIs, design scalable Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and deploy modern workplace technology-all while driving an engaging workplace culture aligned with our company values. We are actively building our operational infrastructure while running it in real-time. To succeed, you must bring a strong "we can figure it out" ownership mindset, thriving in ambiguity as we build, iterate, and elevate the AMER workplace footprint together.
 This is a hybrid role requiring three days in the Boston office. 
 A day in the life (Responsibilities) 
 Vendor Oversight & Program Leadership (The "Product Owner" Approach)
 Act as the strategic owner for the AMER Workplace Experience program, establishing product-like roadmap execution, SLAs, and performance scorecards.
 Direct and manage primary outsourced vendor partners (IFM, janitorial, catering, security, facilities maintenance), ensuring high-service delivery, accountability, and seamless operational handoffs.
 Establish clear key performance indicators (KPIs) and continuous feedback loops to measure and report on workplace performance, employee satisfaction, and space utilization.
 Process Architecture, SOPs & Financial Management
 Build, document, and roll out standardized operational frameworks and SOPs across all AMER sites from the ground up, establishing operational consistency across regions.
 Support financial targets by partnering with leadership on OPEX budgeting, vendor cost management, contract negotiations, and quarterly financial forecasting.
 Drive end-to-end project management for regional workplace initiatives, site refreshes, vendor transitions, and change management strategies.
 Apply scrum methodologies to plan and run workplace initiatives and deliver improvements iteratively across AMER sites.
 Culture, Community & Values Integration
 Partner closely with internal teams-including Inclusion & Diversity, Toast.org, People/HR, and Internal Comms-to design and execute workplace experience strategies that reflect our company values.
 Champion local workplace programming, community involvement, social activations, and sustainability initiatives that turn our physical spaces into hubs of collaboration and purpose.
 Actively embody and champion our One Team mission across every employee touchpoint.
 Workplace Technology, Analytics & Enhancements
 Evaluate, deploy, and manage on-site workplace technologies, including desk/room booking platforms, visitor management, event tech, and occupancy sensors.
 Translate workplace data and space analytics into actionable insights to inform future real estate strategy, space planning, and service offerings.
 What you'll need to thrive (Requirements) 
 Experience: 6+ years of progressive experience in Facilities Management, Workplace Experience, or Corporate Real Estate operations within a fast-growing, matrixed environment.
 Vendor Operations: Proven track record managing complex outsourced vendor programs (IFM/third-party providers), defining contracts, and managing vendor KPIs/SLAs.
 Program Management Mindset: Strong program and project management skills; familiarity with agile methodologies, change management strategies, or serving as a functional "Product Owner" is a major plus.
 Building in Ambiguity: A demonstrated "we can figure it out" attitude. You are comfortable building processes, templates, and SOPs from scratch while keeping daily operations moving flawlessly.
 Cross-Functional Collaboration: Exceptional relationship-building skills with a history of partnering with Inclusion teams, ESG/philanthropic arms, IT, Security, and HR.
 Tech-Savvy: Hands-on experience implementing modern workplace management tools (e.g., Robin, Envoy, Elogbooks, FM Systems) and leveraging analytics dashboards to make data-driven decisions.
 Financial Literacy: Comfort managing program budgets, reviewing purchase orders, tracking vendor invoices, and identifying cost-efficiency opportunities.
 AI at Toast 
 At Toast, one of our company values is that we're hungry to build and learn. We believe learning new AI tools empowers us to build for our customers faster, more independently, and with higher quality. We provide these tools across all disciplines, from Engineering and Product to Sales and Support, and are inspired by how our Toasters are already driving real value with them. The people who thrive here are those who embrace changes that let us build more for our customers; it's a core part of our culture.
 Our Total Rewards Philosophy 
 We strive to provide competitive compensation and benefits programs that help to attract, retain, and motivate the best and brightest people in our industry. Our total rewards package goes beyond great earnings potential and provides the means to a healthy lifestyle with the flexibility to meet Toasters' changing needs. Learn more about our benefits at https://careers.toasttab.com/toast-benefits .
 The base salary range for this role is listed below. The starting salary will be determined based on skills, experience, and geographic location. In addition to base salary, our total rewards components include cash compensation (overtime, bonus/commissions if eligible), equity, and benefits. You can learn more about how we align pay with local labor markets in our Geographic Pay Zone Philosophy . 
 Pay Range
 $101,000 - $162,000 USD 
 How Toast Uses AI in its Hiring Process 
 Throughout the hiring process, our goal is to get to know you. We use AI tools to support our recruiters and interviewers with tasks like note-taking, summarization, and documentation of interviews to ensure they can be fully focused on your conversation. All hiring decisions are made by people. We ask that you complete interviews and assessments on your own, without real-time AI tools, recording, or transcription bots, unless we tell you otherwise in advance. To learn more: https://careers.toasttab.com/ai-in-hiring 
 Our Approach to Hybrid Working 
We embrace a hybrid work model that fosters in-person collaboration while valuing individual needs. Our goal is to build a strong culture of connection as we work together to empower the hospitality community, regardless of location. Please visit the Locations page on our career site to learn more about our in-office expectations by region: https://careers.toasttab.com/locations-toast 
 People Are the Secret Ingredient in Our Recipe for Success 
 At Toast, our employees are our secret ingredient-when they thrive, we thrive. The restaurant industry brings together people with a wide range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives, and we value that same breadth at Toast. We strive to build a culture grounded in authenticity, respect, and humility, where every Toaster has a real opportunity to grow, contribute, and do their best work-raising the bar in delivering exceptional experiences for our customers and each other.
 Apply today! 
 Toast is committed to creating an accessible and inclusive hiring process. As part of this commitment, we strive to provide reasonable accommodations for persons with disabilities to enable them to access the hiring process. title: Customer Support Intern (Summer 2027)
description:
Customer Experience Internship 
 We're Carvana. And we're on a mission to change the way people buy and sell cars. 
 We're a disruptor, an innovator, and a team that's obsessed with creating an unforgettable customer experience. And we believe that mission starts with our people.
 That's where you come in.
 About the internship: the ultimate customer operations bootcamp 
 Forget what you think you know about internships. This isn't your average "get coffee and make copies" gig. This is a 9-week (June 7 - August 6, 2027), paid, immersive bootcamp designed to teach you how to drive customers happy at one of the most innovative companies in business today.
 You'll be embedded in our world-class Customer Experience team, learning from the ground up what it takes to deliver moments of magic to our customers. You'll also get exposure to our Market Operations team, so you can see the driveway and Vending Machine experience up close and appreciate the full, end-to-end car buying journey. Our goal is to give you a 360-degree view of that journey and empower you to make a real, tangible impact.
 This is your chance to be part of a team that's making history, all while building a foundation for your future career.
 We are investing in your development with the ultimate goal of you joining us full-time, so we're looking for candidates who are passionate about building their future at Carvana post-graduation.
 What you'll be doing 
 Learn from the best: You'll go through an accelerated training program designed to give you a deep understanding of our customers, our business, and our secret sauce for success.
 Become a customer champion: You'll be on the front lines, engaging with real customers through live interactions via phone and chat to solve problems and create exceptional experiences.
 See the full journey: Get exposure to the Market Operations side of the business and gain insight into the driveway and Vending Machine experience, so you understand how every step of the car buying process comes together.
 Experience our innovation firsthand: Step away from the desk and see what makes Carvana different. You'll get exclusive tours of our iconic Car Vending Machine and state-of-the-art Inspection Center as you learn about all the teams that bring the customer experience to life.
 Tackle a real business challenge: You and your fellow interns will team up on a hands-on capstone project, presenting your innovative solutions to our senior leadership team at the end of the summer.
 Get a seat at the table: Participate in exclusive lunch & learn sessions with our Executives, get a behind-the-scenes look at our operations, and build a professional network that will last a lifetime.
 Your launchpad: where this internship can take you 
 At the end of the internship, full-time and part-time opportunities are available in our Advocate Operational roles, in either Customer Care or Market Operations. Those are your starting lines, not your finish line.
 At Carvana, the growth doesn't stop in your first role. After 6 months, you become eligible to grow into other teams across the company. We have a ton of internal growth opportunities, and Customer Care is truly the launchpad for them. Because you've spent your time becoming the expert in the experiences we create for customers, you'll bring something every team values: a real understanding of the customer.
 Start: Join as an Advocate in Customer Care or Market Operations after graduation.
 Grow: Become eligible to move into other teams at the 6-month mark.
 Lead the way: Take the customer expertise you've built into whatever career you choose here.
 What you should have 
 We're looking for people who are fired up about our mission and ready to learn. While we don't expect you to have any prior corporate experience, we are looking for:
 Currently enrolled in a four-year university and on track to graduate in Winter 2027 or Spring 2028 (i.e., a rising senior).
 A genuine obsession with helping people and a deep sense of empathy.
 An insatiable curiosity and a desire to understand the "why" behind the "what."
 A top-notch communicator: you're clear, concise, and can talk to just about anyone.
 A true team player who is always willing to lend a hand.
 Resilience and a positive, can-do attitude. You see challenges as opportunities.
 What you'll get 
 A paid, full-time 9-week internship at $20/hr.
 A pathway to a full-time Advocate Operational role in Customer Care or Market Operations, with eligibility to grow into other teams at the 6-month mark. We're not just looking for summer help; we're looking for our next generation of team members.
 A hands-on learning experience that will look amazing on your resume and serve as a launchpad for your career, whether that's with us or beyond.
 Direct mentorship and coaching from a dedicated manager and a team that is invested in your growth.
 Unparalleled access to senior leaders and cross-functional teams.
 An unforgettable summer filled with learning, development, and fun.
 And, of course, some seriously cool Carvana swag.
 Interested? 
 If you're ready to roll up your sleeves, make a difference, and launch your career at a company that's changing the entire car-buying industry, we want to hear from you.

title: Senior Manager / Associate Director, Clinical Quality Assurance
description:
Company Overview: 
 Beam Therapeutics is a biotechnology company committed to establishing the leading, fully integrated platform for precision genetic medicines. To achieve this vision, Beam has assembled a platform with integrated gene editing, delivery and internal manufacturing capabilities. Beam's suite of gene editing technologies is anchored by base editing, a proprietary technology that is designed to enable precise, predictable and efficient single base changes, at targeted genomic sequences, without making double-stranded breaks in the DNA. This has the potential to enable a wide range of therapeutic editing strategies that Beam is using to advance a diversified portfolio of base editing programs. Beam is a values-driven organization committed to its people, cutting-edge science, and a vision of providing life-long cures to patients suffering from serious diseases.
 Position Overview: 
 The Senior Manager / Associate Director of Clinical Quality Assurance (CQA) will provide leadership for the qualification and ongoing quality oversight of CROs and other clinical service providers while providing clinical quality support for assigned studies. This role will partner cross-functionally to implement risk-based vendor oversight, monitor and address vendor quality and compliance risks, and provide pragmatic GCP guidance to study teams. This position will also support quality investigations, audits, CAPAs, and inspection readiness activities to ensure effective sponsor oversight and sustained clinical trial compliance.
 Responsibilities: 
 Lead and manage the qualification and ongoing quality oversight of CROs and other GCP/GCLP/GVP service providers supporting clinical development.
 Maintain a risk-based vendor qualification and oversight framework, including qualification assessments, audits, periodic re-assessments and documentation of vendor quality status.
 Partner with study team members to ensure appropriate quality oversight of associated vendors.
 Determine overall audit strategy / schedule for external GCP/GCLP/GVP vendors, including which audits to conduct internally vs outsource.
 Support QA leadership for significant vendor quality issues, including investigations, RCA, CAPA development/assessment, and effectiveness.
 Support the development of and execute program/study-level risk-based audit plan, including investigator site, vendor and internal process audits.
 Support execution of enterprise-wide GCP inspection readiness strategies and plans.
 Partner cross-functionally to promote effective sponsor oversight of outsourced activities consistent with ICH E6 R3 expectations.
 Serve as the Clinical QA Support for assigned studies and programs.
 Provide quality review of protocols, informed consent forms, investigator brochures, CSRs, and regulatory submission documents as requested.
 Contribute to the continued evolution of the Quality Management System, including oversight and trending of key quality metrics (internal and external).
 Support clinical and QA SOP development efforts.
 Ensure adherence to GxP requirements and SOPs.
 Embody Beam's cultural values and align daily actions with departmental goals and company culture.
 Qualifications: 
 University degree in a scientific discipline/life sciences.
 Experience in a clinical stage biotech company preferred.
 7+ years of relevant experience in clinical/GCP quality. Level will be commensurate with experience.
 3+ years of experience conducting or managing GCP vendor and investigator site audits.
 Professional audit certification (e.g., ASQ CQA, RQAP-GCP) preferred.
 Direct experience qualifying and overseeing CROs and other service providers.
 Strong knowledge of GCP and applicable FDA, EMA, MHRA and ICH requirements.
 Demonstration ability to successfully partner cross-functionally.
 Excellent interpersonal effectiveness, including exceptional communication skills.
 Advanced computer skills, including experience working in Veeva.
 Consistent excellent judgement and pragmatic, risk-based decision making skills.
 Strong team player that has a customer service approach and is solution oriented.
 Attention to detail and the ability to work individually, within a multi-disciplinary team, as well as with external partners and vendors.
 The salary range below reflects the full-time base salary range we expect to pay for this role at the time of posting. Base pay will be determined based on several factors including, but not limited to, relevant experience, education, scope of job, internal comparisons, and market data.
 Beam Pay Range
 $155,000 - $225,000 USD

title: Pharmacy Network Contracting Manager
description:
Who We Are: 
 SmithRx is a rapidly growing, venture-backed Health-Tech company. Our mission is to disrupt the expensive and inefficient Pharmacy Benefit Management (PBM) sector by building a next-generation drug acquisition platform driven by cutting edge technology, innovative cost saving tools, and best-in-class customer service. With hundreds of thousands of members onboarded since 2016, SmithRx has a solution that is resonating with clients all across the country.
 We pride ourselves for our mission-driven and collaborative culture that inspires our employees to do their best work. We believe that the U.S healthcare system is in need of transformation, and we come to work each day dedicated to making that change a reality. At our core, we are guided by our company values:
 Integrity: Our purpose guides our actions and gives us confidence in the path ahead. With unwavering honesty and dependability, we embrace the pressure of challenging the old and exemplify ethical leadership to create the new.
 Courage: We face continuous challenges with grit and resilience. We embrace the discomfort of the unknown by balancing autonomy with empathy, and ownership with vulnerability. We boldly challenge the status quo to keep moving forward-always.
 Together: The success of SmithRx reflects the strength of our partnerships and the commitment of our team. Our shared values bind us together and make us one. When one falls, we all fall; when one rises, we all rise.
 Job Summary:
 The Pharmacy Network Contracting Manager supports the Director of Contracting by serving as the principal process owner for day-to-day pharmacy network contracting operations while partnering closely with Provider Relations to support a strong provider experience at scale. Operating as a highly autonomous individual contributor, this role owns the contracting pipeline and governance, and ensures agreements are negotiated, executed, and accurately configured in SmithRx's claims adjudication system-including reimbursement rates, network participation, and effective dates. The key objective is to improve contracting throughput, consistency, configuration accuracy, and audit readiness while reducing provider friction through clear coordination, communication, and issue resolution.
 What you will do: 
 Lead day-to-day pharmacy contracting operations, serving as the principal subject matter expert and providing mentorship and process guidance to team members.
 Own and optimize the contracting pipeline (intake, prioritization, aging, execution timelines, and deliverables).
 Govern the end-to-end contract lifecycle across new agreements, amendments, renewals, notices, and terminations, including milestone and deadline tracking.
 Lead complex contract negotiation workflows and redline reviews partnering directly with Legal and internal stakeholders to mitigate systemic risks.
 Ensure all reimbursement exhibits, fee schedules, and effective dates are meticulously accurate, approved, and implementation-ready.
 Drive rate loading and network configuration in the claims adjudication system to ensure executed terms are implemented accurately and on time.
 Architect and enforce controls and QA frameworks for rate setup (effective dates, plan/network mapping, reimbursement logic, and exception handling).
 Monitor and manage the rate load/configuration backlog, proactively prioritize urgent builds, mitigate and escalate risks that could impact go-lives or claim outcomes.
 Own post-load validation checkpoints (test claims/spot checks, variance reviews, and issue triage) lead root-cause analysis and ensure corrections are completed.
 Partner strategically with Provider Relations to align contracting timelines, onboarding requirements, and provider-facing communications during contracting and execution.
 Act as the definitive escalation point for contracting- or configuration-related provider escalations; document root causes and drive resolution through and across the appropriate teams.
 Author, govern, and maintain contracting playbooks, SOPs, templates, clause guidance, and standard responses to improve speed, consistency, and provider clarity.
 Drive contract repository and configuration documentation governance (version control, naming standards, executed package completeness, approvals, and change history).
 Leverage data to provide routine reporting on contracting/configuration volume, cycle time, backlog, and issue trends; lead continuous process improvement initiatives to scale operations.
 Architect and maintain a comprehensive contracting knowledge base (FAQs, standard workflows, and escalation paths) to drive internal enablement and elevate the provider experience.
 What you will bring to SmithRx: 
 Bachelor's degree or equivalent relevant experience in PBM, managed care, healthcare contracting, network operations, or provider relations.
 8+ years of experience in pharmacy/provider contracting, PBM network operations, or healthcare contract administration.
 2+ years of experience serving as a principal subject matter expert, process owner and/or managing high-volume contracting workflows.
 Exceptional ability to interpret complex contract language, lead redline negotiations, and strategically identify business, operational, and compliance risks.
 Deep technical understanding of claims adjudication and pharmacy reimbursement configuration (how executed terms translate into system setup).
 Proven experience architecting or overseeing rate loading and configuration accuracy, including effective-date controls and mapping requirements.
 Demonstrated ability to work provider-facing issues through resolution while balancing contracting standards and operational feasibility.
 Advanced cross-functional stakeholder management skills across Provider Relations, Legal, Pricing, Credentialing, Operations, Compliance, and Finance.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to clearly document complex issues, decisions, and next steps.
 Meticulous attention to detail, and the ability to autonomously manage competing priorities and deadlines.
 Advanced proficiency with Excel/Google Sheets and contract tracking/document management practices.
 PBM pharmacy network experience (retail, PSAO/independents, specialty) preferred.
 What SmithRx Offers You:

title: Senior Global Environmental Compliance Specialist
description:
At WHOOP, we're on a mission to unlock and inspire performance for life. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives. Our wearable technology and personalized insights help people optimize recovery, sleep, training, and overall health. As we continue to expand globally, ensuring our products meet evolving environmental regulations is critical to delivering innovative hardware to members around the world.
We're looking for a Senior Global Environmental Compliance Specialist to lead WHOOP's global environmental product compliance. In this role, you'll own the strategy, execution, and continuous evolution of our environmental compliance framework, ensuring our products meet global regulatory requirements throughout the product lifecycle while enabling rapid innovation and worldwide market access.
RESPONSIBILITIES
 - Ensure WHOOP's products meet environmental compliance standards in all current and planned global markets, including regulations such as RoHS, REACH, California Proposition 65, SCIP, POPs, battery, and packaging requirements.
 - Lead regulatory reporting, product declarations, and data submissions to ensure timely and accurate compliance across global markets.
 - Partner with Hardware, Operations and other cross-functional teams to ensure environmental compliance requirements are considered throughout product development, from concept through end of life.
 - Collaborate with Global Supply Management and suppliers to communicate evolving regulatory requirements, collect compliance documentation, and improve supplier readiness.
 - Monitor the global regulatory landscape, assess business impact, and provide recommendations that proactively address emerging environmental requirements.
 - Develop and improve compliance processes, documentation, and operational procedures that scale with WHOOP's product portfolio.
 - Manage environmental compliance data and documentation within compliance management systems, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency through automation.
 - Develop and maintain Bio-compatibility testing standards as appropriate for wearable products. Ensure the team understands requirements applicable to each product and incorporates appropriate bio-compatibility tests early in development.
 - Partner with cross functional teams to satisfy Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) obligations across global markets, including WEEE, Battery, and Packaging waste management registration, data reporting, and Producer Responsibility Organization (PRO) management.
 - Support company initiatives related to voluntary environmental standards and sustainability programs.
QUALIFICATIONS
 - Required: Bachelor's degree in Engineering or Science. Preferred: Materials focused degree or research.
 - At least 5 years of experience managing global environmental compliance for consumer electronics, wearables, or other hardware products.
 - Strong working knowledge of global environmental regulations, including RoHS, REACH, TSCA, California Proposition 65, SCIP, POPs, battery, and packaging requirements.
 - Experience managing environmental compliance data, documentation, and regulatory reporting using compliance management systems such as Greensoft or equivalent tools.
 - Demonstrated ability to interpret complex regulations and translate them into practical engineering and operational requirements.
 - Experience partnering across Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, Quality, and Legal to drive compliance throughout the product lifecycle.
 - Excellent project management, communication, and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
 - Experience supporting voluntary environmental standards or sustainability certification programs.
This role is based in the WHOOP office located in Boston, MA. The successful candidate must be prepared to relocate if necessary to work out of the Boston, MA office. 
Interested in the role, but don't meet every qualification? We encourage you to still apply! At WHOOP, we believe there is much more to a candidate than what is written on paper, and we value character as much as experience. As we continue to build a diverse and inclusive environment, we encourage anyone who is interested in this role to apply.
WHOOP is an Equal Opportunity Employer and participates in E-verify https://www.e-verify.gov/ to determine employment eligibility. It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability.
The WHOOP compensation philosophy is designed to attract, motivate, and retain exceptional talent by offering competitive base salaries, meaningful equity, and consistent pay practices that reflect our mission and core values.
At WHOOP, we view total compensation as the combination of base salary, equity, and benefits, with equity serving as a key differentiator that aligns our employees with the long-term success of the company and allows every member of our corporate team to own part of WHOOP and share in the company's long-term growth and success.
The U.S. base salary range for this full-time position is $140,000 - $195,000. Salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within each range, individual pay is based on factors such as job-related skills, experience, performance, and relevant education or training. 
In addition to the base salary, the successful candidate will also receive benefits and a generous equity package.

 2+ years of experience in healthcare call center environments handling inbound call is required. Outbound call experience is preferred,

title: People Operations Manager
description:
ABOUT AIRWALLEX
Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.
We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.
We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,300 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles https://www.airwallex.com/en-us/operating-principles to see it in full.
ABOUT AIRWALLEX
Airwallex is a global payments and financial infrastructure platform that helps businesses move money globally. Our products span payments, accounts, treasury, cards, spend management and more, giving businesses a simpler way to manage their financial operations across borders.
We're building the future of global finance, and our People & Talent team plays an important role in helping Airwallex scale responsibly. We're looking for thoughtful, hands-on operators who care deeply about employee experience and enjoy turning complex people processes into simple, effective solutions.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
As Manager, People Operations, EMEA, you'll help deliver a high-quality employee experience across a growing and diverse region. You'll combine hands-on operational ownership with process improvement, partnering closely with People Partners, Talent Acquisition, Payroll, Total Rewards, Workplace Experience, Legal and business leaders.
You'll own core employee lifecycle processes across EMEA, support local compliance and benefits administration, maintain accurate people data, and help employees and managers navigate People-related questions. You'll also contribute to the evolution of our regional operating model, identifying opportunities to improve, automate and scale the way we work.
This is a role for someone who is comfortable operating at both the detail level and the regional level: ensuring every onboarding, payroll input and employee query is handled well while also building better systems for the future.
RESPONSIBILITIES
 - Lead and develop the regional People Operations function; own end-to-end employee lifecycle operations (onboarding/orientation, background checks, HRIS data integrity, payroll inputs/changes, benefits and leaves, offboarding) for an EMEA footprint with ~400 employees, with a strong focus on delivery quality and compliance.
 - Drive operational excellence by codifying and maintaining regional SOPs, managing the P&T JIRA helpdesk queue, and setting clear workflows and standards that are consistent with global guidance.
 - Partner cross-functionally with Payroll, IT, and Compliance on accurate and timely transactions, audits, vendor coordination, invoicing/POs, and change control.
 - Run regular data audits and quality checks, identify discrepancies and improve data integrity, reporting and governance.
 - Support the administration and rollout of benefits across relevant EMEA markets, working with internal stakeholders and external providers.
 - Provide operational support for employment changes, leave, probation, right-to-work processes, visas and other country-specific employee matters.
 - Work closely with People Partners and Legal to ensure processes are delivered consistently and in line with relevant local requirements.
 - Identify inefficiencies in manual workflows and drive process improvements, automation and appropriate use of AI.
 - Support regional and global People projects, including implementation of new systems, policies and employee programs.
 - Manage, prioritise and allocate work across People Operations support resources where applicable. Lead and drive a team-based, collaborative environment.
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
 - 6+ years of experience in People Operations, HR Operations or a closely related HR generalist role, ideally in a fast-growing software, internet or fintech company.
 - Strong knowledge of employee lifecycle processes, including onboarding, offboarding, payroll inputs, benefits, HRIS administration and employee data management.
 - Experience supporting employees across multiple EMEA countries (Netherlands, UK, Germany, France, Spain, Italy, Poland, etc.) and working with local employment requirements.
 - Familiarity with payroll processes, including variable compensation such as commissions, bonuses or allowances.
 - A hands-on, detail-oriented approach and the ability to manage high-volume operational work without losing sight of quality.
 - Strong organisational skills, sound judgement and the ability to prioritise competing requests in a fast-moving environment.
 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to work with employees, managers, senior stakeholders and external providers.
 - A track record of improving processes, documenting ways of working and reducing manual effort. Experience using AI to drive improvements is highly preferred.
 - High standards of confidentiality, discretion and data accuracy.
 - The ability to operate independently, solve problems pragmatically and make progress despite ambiguity.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
 - Familiarity with BambooHR, Deel, Jira, Confluence, Lattice, Slack and Google Workspace.
 - Experience supporting EOR populations or employees across multiple legal entities.
 - Experience with HR systems implementation, workflow automation, reporting or AI-enabled process improvement.
 - Experience partnering with Workplace Experience or supporting office-based employee programs.
 - Professional HR qualification or equivalent practical experience.
YOU'LL THRIVE HERE IF
 - You enjoy working across countries, cultures and time zones and can adapt your approach to different local contexts.
 - You're comfortable moving between detailed execution and broader process improvement.
 - You default to action, learn quickly and course-correct when priorities change.
 - You communicate clearly, flag issues early and take ownership through to resolution.
 - You care about making complex processes easier for employees and managers.
 - You're low-ego, collaborative and focused on achieving the right outcome for the business and our people.
APPLICANT SAFETY POLICY: FRAUD AND THIRD-PARTY RECRUITERS
To protect you from recruitment scams, please be aware that Airwallex will not ask for bank details, sensitive ID numbers (i.e. passport), or any form of payment during the application or interview process. All official communication will come from an @airwallex.com http://airwallex.com email address. Please apply only through careers.airwallex.com http://careers.airwallex.com or our official LinkedIn page.
Airwallex does not accept unsolicited resumes from search firms/recruiters. Airwallex will not pay any fees to search firms/recruiters if a candidate is submitted by a search firm/recruiter unless an agreement has been entered into with respect to specific open position(s). Search firms/recruiters submitting resumes to Airwallex on an unsolicited basis shall be deemed to accept this condition, regardless of any other provision to the contrary.
EQUAL OPPORTUNITY
Airwallex is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and anyone seeking employment at Airwallex is considered based on merit, qualifications, competence and talent. We don't regard color, religion, race, national origin, sexual orientation, ancestry, citizenship, sex, marital or family status, disability, gender, or any other legally protected status when making our hiring decisions. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

title: Senior Strategy & Operations Manager
description:
WE POWER PEOPLE'S PROGRESS.
At Preply, we're all about creating life-changing learning experiences. We help people discover the magic of the perfect tutor, craft a personalised learning journey, and stay motivated to keep growing. Our approach is human-led, tech-enabled - and it's creating real impact.
We've just reached unicorn status with a $150M Series D, accelerating our vision to transform education through human-led, AI-enhanced learning. Today, 100,000+ tutors teach 90+ languages to learners in 180 countries - and we're only getting started. As a category-defining company, we're shaping what the future of learning looks like at global scale.
Every Preply lesson sparks change, fuels ambition, and drives progress that matters. Joining Preply means helping define the future of education at global scale, and building something that truly matters for millions of people, every day.
MEET THE TEAM
We're building a central Strategy team at the heart of Preply, driving clarity, focus, and disciplined execution across the company.
Reporting directly to our Director of Strategy & Operations, the Strategy team will work with the executive team to define company direction, shape strategic priorities, and lead the cross-functional initiatives that turn strategy into measurable business outcomes.
As Preply scales globally and prepares for its next growth chapter, we're looking for Senior Strategy & Operations Managers to own strategic transformation projects - from improving customer retention and lifetime value to expanding beyond languages into new learning categories. You'll work on projects that have genuine impact across the entire business.
WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING
1. STRATEGIC INITIATIVES & TRANSFORMATION
 - Own strategic transformation projects end-to-end, typically spanning 3-12 months, with real business impact across the company.
 - Lead cross-functional teams to define strategy, scope workstreams, and drive accountability to outcomes. Examples include improving customer retention and reducing churn, growing customer lifetime value through better monetization and engagement, and evaluating new market segments and product offerings as we expand beyond languages.
 - Conduct data-driven analysis and market research to identify growth opportunities, diagnose root causes of business challenges, and recommend new strategic directions.
 - Assess and prioritize market opportunities, potential partnerships, or M&A targets based on strategic fit and business impact.
2. CROSS-FUNCTIONAL LEADERSHIP & EXECUTION
 - Influence senior leaders without formal authority - navigating competing priorities, building shared ownership, and driving decisions rather than endless discussion.
 - Coordinate complex initiatives across product, marketing, operations, and other functions - managing stakeholder alignment and proactively flagging and resolving risks.
 - Translate ambiguity into clear scopes and action plans. Manage parallel workstreams while maintaining focus on measurable business outcomes, not just activity.
3. EXECUTIVE COMMUNICATION & INSIGHT
 - Produce clear, data-backed narratives for leadership and the board - tailoring messaging for different audiences (CEO vs. functional leads) and communicating complex ideas with precision.
 - Present findings and recommendations with both confidence and presence - you're a thought partner in the room, not just a presenter of decks.
WHAT YOU NEED TO SUCCEED
 - 7+ years of experience in strategy, operations, or leading cross-functional strategic initiatives - ideally in high-growth tech or marketplace environments.
 - Proven track record owning strategic projects or transformation initiatives from scope to delivery - not just planning or analysis.
 - Strong commercial acumen - understanding of marketplace dynamics, business models, monetization, and growth mechanics. Ability to connect strategy to financial outcomes.
 - Exceptional strategic and analytical thinking - structures ambiguous problems with frameworks, prioritizes ruthlessly based on strategic logic, connects insights to business outcomes.
 - Outstanding ability to influence across functions - can challenge upward constructively, build buy-in without authority, and manage competing stakeholder interests diplomatically.
 - Excellent executive presence and communication - comfortable presenting complex ideas with clarity and presence in high-stakes forums. Written and verbal communication are equally strong.
 - AI fluency - You actively use AI to accelerate analysis, research, and strategic work. You can name specific tools and articulate how they've changed your approach.
 - Action-oriented and resourceful - You're comfortable navigating ambiguity and moving with imperfect information. You drive decisions, not just discussions.
 - Attention to detail and strong organizational skills - You deliver polished work and follow through on commitments without being asked.
 - Based in Barcelona or London, with a preference for Barcelona.
WHY YOU'LL LOVE IT AT PREPLY:
 - An open, collaborative, dynamic and diverse culture;
 - A generous monthly allowance for lessons on http://preply.comPreply.com http://Preply.com, Learning & Development budget and time off for your self-development;
 - A competitive financial package with equity, leave allowance and health insurance;
 - Not in Barcelona? We offer an attractive relocation package to join us in our Preply Barcelona Hub
 - Access to free mental health support platforms;
 - Access to Gympass-partnered wellness and gym centers to promote and support well-being and physical health;
 - The opportunity to unlock the potential of learners and tutors through language learning and teaching in 175 countries (and counting!)
OUR PRINCIPLES
 - Care to change the world - We are passionate about our work and care deeply about its impact to be life changing.
 - We do it for learners - For both Preply and tutors, learners are why we do what we do. Every day we focus on empowering tutors to deliver an exceptional learning experience.
 - Keep perfecting - To create an outstanding customer experience, we focus on simplicity, smoothness, and enjoyment, continually perfecting it as every detail matters.
 - Now is the time - In a fast-paced world, it matters how quickly we act. Now is the time to make great things happen.
 - Disciplined execution - What makes us disciplined is the excellence in our execution. We set clear goals, focus on what matters, and utilize our resources efficiently.
 - Dive deep - We leverage business acumen and curiosity to investigate disparities between numbers and stories, unlocking meaningful insights to guide our decisions.
 - Growth mindset - We proactively seek growth opportunities and believe today's best performance becomes tomorrow's starting point. We humbly embrace feedback and learn from setbacks.
 - Raise the bar - We raise our performance standards continuously, alongside each new hire and promotion. We build diverse and high-performing teams that can make a real difference.
 - Challenge, disagree and commit - We value open and candid communication, even when we don't fully agree. We speak our minds, challenge when necessary, and fully commit to decisions once made.
 - One Preply - We prioritize collaboration, inclusion, and the success of our team over personal ambitions. Together, we support and celebrate each other's progress.
DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSION
Preply.com http://Preply.com is committed to creating an inclusive environment where people of diverse backgrounds can thrive. We believe that the presence of different opinions and viewpoints is a key ingredient for our success as a multicultural Ed-Tech company. That means that Preply will consider all applications for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, age or veteran status.

title: Senior Manager, Pharmacy Operations (Prior Authorization)
description:
Company Overview:
 Blink Health is the fastest growing healthcare technology company that builds products to make prescriptions accessible and affordable to everybody. Our two primary products - BlinkRx and Quick Save - remove traditional roadblocks within the current prescription supply chain, resulting in better access to critical medications and improved health outcomes for patients. 
 BlinkRx is the world's first pharma-to-patient cloud that offers a digital concierge service for patients who are prescribed branded medications. Patients benefit from transparent low prices, free home delivery, and world-class support on this first-of-its-kind centralized platform. With BlinkRx, never again will a patient show up at the pharmacy only to discover that they can't afford their medication, their doctor needs to fill out a form for them, or the pharmacy doesn't have the medication in stock. 
We are a highly collaborative team of builders and operators who invent new ways of working in an industry that historically has resisted innovation. Join us!
 This role is based in Pittsburgh, PA (Robinson Township); candidates must reside locally or be willing to relocate. 
 The Opportunity 
 The Patient Services Operations team is at the forefront of the company mission to bring affordable prices and deliver the best experience for all of our patients. The Senior Manager, Pharmacy Operations leads prior authorization production within a fast-growing hub pharmacy. This position is a mid-senior level role for a hands-on operator who thrives in ambiguity, builds scalable processes, and develops high-performing hourly teams.
 You will own day-to-day execution and performance outcomes while partnering cross-functionally to evolve workflows, technology, and operating models as the business scales. Success in this role requires balancing tactical execution with strategic thinking-driving results today while building systems that work tomorrow.
 Responsibilities 
 Leading with Operational Excellence
 Own end-to-end production performance for prior authorization workflows, ensuring consistent delivery against SLAs, turnaround time, quality, and productivity targets.
 Establish and evolve operating rhythms to manage volume variability, capacity planning, backlog health, and risk.
 Identify bottlenecks and failure points across people, process, and technology; drive pragmatic, scalable solutions.
 Building, Developing & Scaling Talent
 Hire, lead, and develop a high-performing hourly workforce, including front-line specialists and team leads.
 Set clear performance expectations and coach employees through regular 1:1s, real-time feedback, and structured performance management.
 Use performance data and direct observation to identify skill gaps and deliver targeted coaching and training.
 Create an environment of accountability, engagement, and continuous improvement.
 Build bench strength and leadership capability to support growth and operational resilience.
 Operating with Data & Accountability
 Use data to drive staffing/scheduling, prioritization, and performance management.
 Own and continuously improve key operational metrics, including SLA attainment, cycle time, productivity, quality, rework, and attrition.
 Translate complex operational data into clear insights and recommendations for leadership and cross-functional partners.
 Partnering Cross-Functionally to Improve Systems
 Partner closely with Operations leadership to align production outcomes with broader company goals.
 Collaborate with Product and Engineering teams to improve workflows, tooling, automation, and system usability.
 Act as the voice of PA operations by documenting requirements, identifying impact, and validating solutions.
 Support pilots, launches, and change management efforts for new processes and technology.
 Thriving in a Startup Environment
 Roll up your sleeves to solve problems directly when needed, while also building repeatable systems.
 Navigate ambiguity, shifting priorities, and rapid growth with a solutions-oriented mindset.
 Balance speed with quality, ensuring scalability without sacrificing execution.
 A successful applicant will fit the following criteria: 
 Experience: 5+ years of managerial experience scaling operations/production in a start-up and/or high-volume/growth company (healthcare tech, prior authorization, and/or pharmacy experience preferred); Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Operations Management, or a related field.
 Team Management: Demonstrated success leading and developing high-performing hourly teams through hiring, coaching, and performance management.
 Operational Management: Experience owning and presenting SLAs, KPIs, key metrics, and operational reporting.
 Problem Solving: Exceptional problem-solving skills and demonstrated experience delivering results using operational excellence best practice methodologies (Lean/Six Sigma certification preferred).
 Detail-Oriented: Strong attention to detail - quickly become an expert in new areas, ask the right questions, and connect dots to ensure operational excellence.

title: Senior Security Analyst, Security Risk Management
location: Seattle Office; Raleigh Office; San Francisco HQ; New York City Office
description:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We're dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid's network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.
ABOUT THE TEAM:
The Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) team is part of Plaid's security organization, focused on enabling the business by proactively managing information security risks and maintaining effective controls.
Our mission is to reduce the likelihood and impact of security risks while operating a robust assurance program that builds trust with our customers, consumers, and data partners.We partner closely across the company to ensure Plaid's platform remains secure, resilient, and aligned with industry and regulatory expectations.Security risk management is how Plaid makes informed security trade-offs-we identify and analyze the risks that could materially affect the business, make sure the right owners decide what to do about them, and turn that picture into reporting leadership and the board can act on.
ABOUT THE ROLE:
 - You will run security risk assessments end-to-end within Plaid's security risk management program-intake, scenario-based analysis, treatment decisions, and monitoring across security, infrastructure, and product risk.
 - You will work with engineering SMEs and risk owners on risks ranging from over-privileged access and supply-chain gaps to product abuse and AI adoption, giving owners a clear, defensible basis for accepting or mitigating each one.
 - You will build quarterly security risk reporting and the security risk content in leadership and board materials.
 - You will help integrate security risk into enterprise risk management, so it is tracked and weighed alongside the rest of the business.
 - You will help mature the program as its scope grows, and operate as an AI power user who automates the work so it scales.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
 - Run Security Risk Assessments: Triage intake, run scenario-based risk analyses with engineering SMEs, score initial and residual risk, and drive risk owners to a documented treatment decision. Your analysis turns vague concerns into decisions leadership can stand behind.
 - Build Quarterly Risk Reporting: Gather updates on material risks, prepare the Security Risk Review, and build the security risk content for executive and board decks. Your reporting gives leadership a clear, current view of where security risk sits and what's being done about it.
 - Integrate Security Risk into ERM: Partner with enterprise risk stakeholders to map security risks into the enterprise taxonomy, align rating scales, and keep the registers in sync. Your work puts security risk alongside business risk instead of in a silo.
 - Mature the Program: Help evolve the risk framework, register, key risk indicators, and risk-owner self-service as the program's scope grows. Your work moves the program from tracking risks to measuring and reducing them.
 - Support FedRAMP 20x Risk Decisions: Help make sure unmet FedRAMP rules and KSI gaps carry a documented risk explanation and senior-official acceptance in the Security Decision Record, consistent with the risk register. Your work keeps Plaid's FedRAMP risk posture defensible to agencies and assessors.
 - Scale Through AI and Automation: Build AI skills and automations for intake triage, first-draft risk analyses, register hygiene, and report generation-and share them across the team. Your approach lets the program cover more risk without adding headcount.
QUALIFICATIONS:
Must haves:
 - Security risk assessment:
 - Experience running scenario-based analyses of technical risks (cloud, IAM, software supply chain, application and product) using NIST SP 800-30, FAIR, or a comparable method.
 - Technical depth to engage engineers on architecture and controls, and to tell a real exposure from a hypothetical one.
 - Risk program maturity and ERM integration:
 - Experience building or maturing a security risk program-methodology, register, treatment and exception workflow, and key risk indicators.
 - Experience integrating security risk into an enterprise risk management program.
 - Risk reporting and executive communication:
 - Experience preparing quarterly risk reporting and building security risk content for executive and board decks.
 - Ability to turn technical risk into a concise executive narrative without overstating or hand-waving.
 - Security and compliance knowledge:
 - Working knowledge of NIST 800-53, NIST CSF, ISO 27001, and SOC 2, and how risk management feeds each.
 - AI fluency and tooling:
 - Power user who has built AI skills, agents, or automations that materially increase risk-program throughput-and who shares what works with the team.
Nice to have:
 - Hands-on FedRAMP 20x experience, including Security Decision Record reporting for rules and Key Security Indicators (SDR-CSO-FRR, SDR-CSX-KSI).

To support that mission, we seek to build a diverse team of driven individuals who care deeply about making the financial ecosystem more equitable. title: Associate Director, Clinical Supply Chain Planning
description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.
 Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor-all in service of patients.
 The Opportunity: 
 Collaborating with product leads and study managers, will ensure global clinical demand for RevMed and Non Rev-Med commercial products is accurately reflected within the N-side system on a monthly basis as part of DnOP process.
 Drive business process standardization, implementation, and training on new processes.
 Lead end-to-end clinical supply planning for assigned clinical programs and studies, from study start-up through closeout.
 Support the development of global clinical supply strategies aligned with clinical protocols, enrollment assumptions, dosing regimens, country activation plans, and program timelines.
 Build and maintain clinical supply forecasts, translating clinical demand into manufacturing, packaging, labeling, distribution, and inventory requirements.
 Develop scenario analyses and supply models to evaluate enrollment changes, dose modifications, cohort expansions, geographic changes, and other protocol or operational assumptions.
 Establish appropriate inventory and safety-stock strategies to maintain continuity of supply while minimizing waste, obsolescence, and expiry risk.
 Monitor inventory levels, consumption, enrollment trends, expiry dates, and other supply indicators and proactively identify potential shortages or excess inventory.
 Drive continuous improvement of clinical supply planning processes, systems, metrics, and ways of working.
 Contribute to performance management, budgeting, and long-range clinical supply planning.
 Provide guidance and subject-matter expertise to colleagues and cross-functional partners on clinical supply planning and execution.
 Required Skills, Experience and Education: 
 Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Life Sciences, Engineering, Business, or a related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
 Typically 8+ years of relevant experience in pharmaceutical or biotechnology supply chain, including substantial experience supporting clinical-stage programs.
 Demonstrated experience independently managing clinical supply planning for complex, global clinical studies. Oncology experience preferred.
 Strong understanding of clinical development and the clinical supply lifecycle, including forecasting, manufacturing planning, packaging and labeling, distribution, depot management, inventory management, and returns/reconciliation.
 Experience developing demand forecasts and scenario models based on enrollment, dosing, treatment duration, randomization, site activation, and other clinical assumptions.
 N-side forecasting tool experience.
 Working knowledge of IRT/RTSM systems and their role in clinical supply management.
 Understanding of GMP/GDP requirements and relevant regulatory expectations governing clinical trial materials.
 Demonstrated ability to identify supply risks, evaluate tradeoffs, and develop practical mitigation strategies in a dynamic clinical development environment.
 Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills with attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple studies and competing priorities.
 Excellent communication and stakeholder-management skills, with demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional teams without direct authority.
 Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment where study assumptions and priorities may change rapidly.
 Preferred Skills: 
 Experience supporting multiple clinical programs or studies simultaneously across different phases of development.
 Experience with oncology or other complex clinical development programs.
 Experience with global clinical trials and country-specific supply requirements.
 Familiarity with clinical supply planning, ERP, inventory management, and forecasting systems.
 Experience establishing clinical supply KPIs, dashboards, or operational performance metrics.
 Demonstrated experience improving clinical supply processes and implementing scalable planning practices.
